title: SDDC Manager Authentication Failure Threshold
description: Repeated SDDC Manager login failures from a single source in a short window. SDDC Manager is the top of the VCF management hierarchy — it can orchestrate vCenter, ESXi, and NSX simultaneously — so brute-force activity against it warrants the same urgency as against a domain controller.

data_sources.name: SDDC Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Login failure events.

detection_logic: Counts SDDC Manager login failures per source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<sddc_manager_sourcetype> event="LoginFailed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count dc(user) as users by _time src
| where count>=8
tuning_guidance: Tune out known automation/API-client sources with occasional credential-rotation failures.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and block if unrecognized.
Check for a subsequent success (VCF-002).
response_guidance: Block the source at the management-network boundary.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful SDDC Manager Login Following Repeated Failures
description: A successful SDDC Manager login for a user/source that had five or more failures in the preceding window. Given SDDC Manager's position atop the VCF management hierarchy, this ranks among the single highest-priority detections in the entire catalogue.

data_sources.name: SDDC Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Login success/failure sequence.

detection_logic: Joins a failed-login threshold search with a subsequent success for the same user/source within a bounded window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<sddc_manager_sourcetype> event IN ("LoginFailed","LoginSucceeded")
| eval outcome=if(event="LoginSucceeded","success","fail")
| sort 0 user src _time
| streamstats time_window=15m count(eval(outcome="fail")) as failures by user src
| where outcome="success" AND failures>=5
| table _time, user, src, failures
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate given how tightly SDDC Manager access should normally be scoped.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Immediately check for subsequent workload-domain, host-commission, or credential changes in the same session (VCF-011+).
response_guidance: Disable the account, disconnect the session, and audit every action taken during it before doing anything else.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SDDC Manager Login From First-Seen Source IP
description: A successful SDDC Manager login originated from a source IP not previously seen managing this deployment.

investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the new source.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed.

title: Component Downgrade via Lifecycle Manager
description: A VCF component (SDDC Manager, vCenter, NSX, or ESXi) was upgraded to a version lower than the currently running one, a well-established technique to reintroduce known vulnerabilities across the security-sensitive management stack.

data_sources.name: SDDC Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Upgrade events with before/after version.

detection_logic: Compares old and new version on upgrade-completion events and flags any decrease.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<sddc_manager_sourcetype> event="UpgradeCompleted"
| eval downgrade=if(old_version>new_version, 1, 0)
| where downgrade=1
| table _time, user, target_component, old_version, new_version
tuning_guidance: Alert on every confirmed downgrade; rare legitimate case is recovery from a bad release.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Identify who initiated the downgrade and the bundle's source.
response_guidance: Revert to the latest known-good version and audit the component for activity that occurred while downgraded.

investigation_steps: Treat as a live supply-chain-attack incident.
Verify no bundles have been downloaded from the unapproved depot since the change.

title: NSX Distributed Firewall Deny Rule Changed to Allow
description: An existing DFW rule's action was changed from deny/drop to allow, directly opening a previously-blocked network path — one of the highest-value microsegmentation-bypass signals in the catalogue.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Rule action-change events.

detection_logic: Filters DFW rule modification events where the action changed from deny/drop to allow.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="DfwRuleModified" field_changed="action"
| where old_action IN ("deny","drop") AND new_action="allow"
| table _time, user, rule_id, source, destination, service
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside a deliberate, ticketed segmentation change; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Identify the source/destination/service this now permits and whether that path was previously restricted for a reason.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized; investigate for lateral-movement activity that may already have used the new path.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: NSX Distributed Firewall Rule Source/Destination Broadened
description: An existing DFW rule's source or destination scope was broadened (e.g. from a specific security group to Any), expanding which traffic the rule's action applies to.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Rule source/destination modification events.

detection_logic: Filters DFW rule modification events for source/destination changes where the new value is 'Any' or a broader group.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="DfwRuleModified" field_changed IN ("source","destination")
| where new_value="Any"
| table _time, user, rule_id, field_changed, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets.
investigation_steps: Assess the resulting exposure for the affected rule's action.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ANY/ANY Allow Rule Introduced
description: A DFW rule was created or modified to allow ANY source to ANY destination on ANY service, effectively disabling microsegmentation for the scope that rule applies to — treat as Critical per the specification's own guidance.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Rule creation/modification events matching an ANY/ANY/ANY pattern.

detection_logic: Filters DFW rule creation/modification events where source, destination, and service are all Any and action is allow.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("DfwRuleCreated","DfwRuleModified")
| where source="Any" AND destination="Any" AND service="Any" AND action="allow"
| table _time, user, rule_id
tuning_guidance: Essentially no legitimate case for a production ANY/ANY/ANY allow rule; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Determine the rule's effective scope (which segments/groups it actually applies to given rule ordering).
response_guidance: Remove immediately and investigate for any traffic that traversed via this rule while active.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: NSX Distributed Firewall Logging Disabled on Rule
description: Per-rule logging was disabled on a DFW rule, which given DFW logging is a primary telemetry source for east-west traffic visibility, blinds monitoring for whatever traffic pattern that rule governs.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Per-rule logging configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters DFW rule modification events where the logging flag is disabled.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="DfwRuleModified" field_changed="logged" new_value="false"
| table _time, user, rule_id
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate log-volume-reduction efforts.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification, especially for rules governing sensitive segments.
response_guidance: Re-enable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: NSX Distributed Firewall Globally Disabled
description: The Distributed Firewall was globally disabled for a cluster/domain, removing microsegmentation enforcement entirely for every workload in scope.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Global DFW state-change events.

detection_logic: Filters global DFW disablement events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="DfwGloballyDisabled"
| table _time, user, scope
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences given the total loss of enforcement.
investigation_steps: Treat as a critical live incident.
response_guidance: Re-enable immediately and investigate the account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Security Group / Dynamic Membership Criteria Changed
description: An NSX security group's dynamic membership criteria was changed, which — since DFW rules are frequently scoped to security groups rather than individual VMs — can silently pull additional workloads into (or push protected workloads out of) a policy's effective scope without ever touching a firewall rule directly.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Security group criteria-change events.

detection_logic: Filters security group membership-criteria change events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="GroupCriteriaChanged"
| table _time, user, group_name, old_criteria, new_criteria
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate policy tuning.
investigation_steps: Determine which DFW rules reference this group and assess the resulting scope change.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Sensitive VM Moved to Broader Security Group
description: A VM tagged as sensitive/Tier-0 was moved from a restrictive security group into a broader one (e.g. from 'Isolated-DC' to 'General-Workloads'), which — via whatever DFW rules reference the new group — can dramatically increase the VM's network exposure without any firewall rule itself changing.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Group membership change events joined against a sensitive-VM tag lookup.

detection_logic: Joins group membership-change events against a sensitive-VM tag lookup and flags moves into broader groups.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="GroupMembershipChanged"
| lookup sensitive_vm_tags.csv vm_name OUTPUT is_sensitive
| where is_sensitive=1
| lookup group_restrictiveness.csv new_group OUTPUT restrictiveness_rank
| lookup group_restrictiveness.csv old_group OUTPUT old_restrictiveness_rank AS old_group
| where restrictiveness_rank<old_restrictiveness_rank
| table _time, user, vm_name, old_group, new_group
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained sensitive-VM tag lookup and a group-restrictiveness ranking; high value once available.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident given the sensitivity tagging.
Verify the new DFW exposure resulting from this membership change.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Isolation/Quarantine Tag Removed from VM
description: A security tag used to isolate or quarantine a VM (e.g. after an incident-response containment action) was removed, restoring network connectivity to a VM that was deliberately isolated — worth the highest scrutiny given this directly reverses a containment control.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Tag removal events for isolation/quarantine-tagged VMs.

detection_logic: Filters tag-removal events for tags matching an isolation/quarantine naming pattern.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="TagRemoved"
| where match(tag, "(?i)(isolat|quarantine|contain)")
| table _time, user, vm_name, tag
tuning_guidance: Confirm against the incident-response ticket that authorized the removal, if any; alert on all occurrences otherwise.
investigation_steps: Verify this removal is part of an authorized incident-closure process.
If unconfirmed, treat the VM as still potentially compromised.
response_guidance: Re-apply the isolation tag immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Gateway Firewall Rule Weakened on Tier-0/Tier-1
description: A Gateway Firewall rule on a Tier-0 or Tier-1 gateway was modified to broaden source, destination, or service scope, or its action was changed from drop/reject to allow — gateway firewalls sit at the north-south perimeter, so a weakened rule here has a larger blast radius than a DFW rule change.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.path: NSX Manager gateway firewall policy log
data_sources.description: Gateway firewall rule change events on Tier-0/Tier-1 gateways.

detection_logic: Filters gateway firewall rule-modification events where the new configuration is broader or the action moved toward allow.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="GatewayFirewallRuleModified"
| where new_action="allow" AND old_action!="allow"
| table _time, user, gateway, rule_id, old_action, new_action
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets; north-south perimeter changes warrant tighter approval workflows than east-west ones.
investigation_steps: Determine the gateway's role (internet edge vs. inter-tenant) to assess exposure.
Check who approved the change.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized; escalate as a perimeter-security incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Gateway Firewall Disabled on Tier-0/Tier-1
description: The Gateway Firewall was globally disabled on a Tier-0 or Tier-1 gateway, removing north-south perimeter filtering entirely.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.path: NSX Manager gateway firewall config log
data_sources.description: Global gateway firewall enable/disable events.

detection_logic: Filters gateway-firewall global status-change events where the new status is disabled.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="GatewayFirewallStatusChanged" status="disabled"
| table _time, user, gateway
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; maintenance windows should be documented exceptions, not silent baseline.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Determine what traffic the gateway now permits unfiltered.
response_guidance: Re-enable immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: NAT Rule Added Exposing Internal Workload
description: A DNAT rule was created mapping an external IP/port to an internal workload that previously had no external reachability, potentially exposing an internal service to the internet or creating a covert egress/ingress path.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: DNAT rule creation events.

detection_logic: Filters DNAT rule-creation events joined against a known-exposed-workload baseline to flag new mappings.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="NatRuleCreated" nat_type="DNAT"
| lookup known_exposed_workloads.csv internal_ip OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, gateway, external_ip, internal_ip, translated_port
tuning_guidance: Maintain a baseline of intentionally-exposed workloads to reduce noise.
investigation_steps: Verify the internal workload and confirm business justification for external exposure.
Check whether the exposed port maps to a known-vulnerable service.
response_guidance: Remove the NAT rule if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: NAT Rule Deleted Removing Protective Translation
description: A SNAT/DNAT rule was deleted; if the rule was masking internal addressing or restricting inbound reachability, its removal can change the network's effective exposure.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: NAT rule deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters NAT rule-deletion events for correlation with subsequent connectivity changes.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="NatRuleDeleted"
| table _time, user, gateway, rule_id
tuning_guidance: Correlate with change tickets; low standalone severity but useful as a building block for NSX-021-style pattern detection.
investigation_steps: Confirm the deletion was authorized.
Assess resulting connectivity changes.
response_guidance: Restore if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Static Route Injected on Tier-0 Gateway
description: A static route was added to a Tier-0 gateway, potentially redirecting traffic for a given subnet toward an attacker-controlled next-hop for interception or exfiltration.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Static route creation events on Tier-0 gateways.

detection_logic: Filters static-route creation events on Tier-0 gateways joined against a known-next-hop baseline.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="StaticRouteCreated" gateway_tier="Tier-0"
| lookup known_next_hops.csv next_hop OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, gateway, network, next_hop
tuning_guidance: Maintain a known-next-hop baseline; Tier-0 static routes change infrequently in most environments.
investigation_steps: Verify the next-hop address is a legitimate, expected router/appliance.
Check what traffic now flows through this route.
response_guidance: Remove immediately if the next-hop is unrecognized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: BGP Neighbor Added or Route Redistribution Changed
description: A new BGP neighbor was configured on a Tier-0 gateway, or a route-redistribution policy was changed — both can be used to inject or withdraw routes across the environment's dynamic routing domain.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: BGP neighbor and redistribution-policy change events.

detection_logic: Filters BGP configuration-change events for new neighbors or redistribution-policy modifications.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("BgpNeighborAdded","RedistributionPolicyChanged")
| table _time, user, gateway, neighbor_ip, change_type
tuning_guidance: Confirm against network change tickets; BGP topology changes are typically rare and planned.
investigation_steps: Verify the neighbor IP belongs to an authorized upstream/peer router.
Review the redistribution policy diff for scope changes.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized neighbors/policies immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Segment Created and Attached to Tier-1 Without Change Ticket Correlation
description: A new overlay segment (logical switch) was created and attached to a Tier-1 gateway; unauthorized segment creation can be used to stand up an attacker-controlled network for staging or C2 relay reachable from compromised workloads.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Segment creation and Tier-1 attachment events.

detection_logic: Lists segment-creation events for manual correlation against change management; primarily a building-block detection for volume-based follow-on rules.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="SegmentCreated"
| table _time, user, segment_name, tier1_gateway, transport_zone
tuning_guidance: Standalone this is low-value due to routine use; pair with NSX-026 for the higher-confidence mass-creation variant.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the new segment.
Check what workloads get attached to it subsequently.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass Segment Creation in Short Window
description: An unusually large number of segments were created in a short window by a single user or API principal, consistent with an attacker or automation script rapidly building out attacker-controlled network infrastructure.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Segment creation events aggregated per actor per time window.

detection_logic: Counts segment-creation events per user within a rolling window and flags counts above a threshold.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="SegmentCreated"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(segment_name) AS segment_count values(segment_name) AS segments by _time, user
| where segment_count>=10
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known automation/IaC service accounts (Terraform, Ansible).
investigation_steps: Identify whether the actor is a known IaC pipeline.
If not, treat as a live incident.
response_guidance: Freeze the account and remove unauthorized segments.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Edge Node Configuration or Uplink Changed
description: An NSX Edge transport node's uplink or configuration was changed outside of a maintenance window, which can disrupt north-south connectivity for every workload behind the affected Tier-0/Tier-1 gateways.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.path: NSX Manager Edge node config log
data_sources.description: Edge transport-node configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters Edge node configuration-change events outside the declared maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="EdgeNodeConfigChanged"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user, edge_node, change_type
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintenance-window lookup; without one, expect routine changes to trigger.
investigation_steps: Confirm the change against a maintenance ticket.
Assess resulting connectivity impact across dependent gateways.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes; failover to a healthy Edge node if impact is ongoing.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.004: Application or System Exploitation

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Edge Cluster Failover or Multiple Edge Nodes Down
description: Multiple NSX Edge nodes within the same cluster transitioned to a down/degraded state in a short window, which can indicate a targeted denial-of-service against the north-south routing/firewall layer or a destructive administrative action.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Edge node status-change events aggregated per cluster per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct Edge nodes transitioning to down/degraded status within a cluster within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="EdgeNodeStatusChanged" status IN ("down","degraded")
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats dc(edge_node) AS down_count values(edge_node) AS nodes by _time, edge_cluster
| where down_count>=2
tuning_guidance: Correlate with planned maintenance/upgrade windows to suppress expected rolling-reboot noise.
investigation_steps: Check for a concurrent VCF Lifecycle Manager upgrade task.
If none, treat as a live availability incident.
response_guidance: Engage infrastructure on-call; failover traffic to healthy Edge nodes.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.004: Application or System Exploitation

author: Threat Detection Library

title: IDS/IPS Signature Set Downgraded or Disabled
description: NSX Distributed IDS/IPS was disabled for a security group/segment, or its active signature profile was downgraded to a weaker set, removing intrusion-detection coverage for the affected workloads.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: IDS/IPS profile-assignment and enable/disable events.

detection_logic: Filters IDS/IPS configuration events where protection is disabled or a profile downgrade is detected.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("IdsProfileChanged","IdsDisabled")
| table _time, user, scope, old_profile, new_profile
tuning_guidance: Alert on all disable events; downgrade detection requires a profile-strength ranking lookup.
investigation_steps: Determine why IDS/IPS was disabled/downgraded for this scope.
Check subsequent traffic to the affected workloads for signs of exploitation attempts.
response_guidance: Re-enable/restore the profile immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IDS/IPS High-Severity Signature Triggered
description: NSX Distributed IDS/IPS raised a high or critical-severity signature match against east-west traffic between workloads, indicating a likely active exploitation attempt already inside the segmented network.

data_sources.name: NSX IDS/IPS Event Log
data_sources.path: NSX Manager distributed IDS/IPS event log
data_sources.description: Signature-match events with severity and CVE/rule metadata.

detection_logic: Filters IDS/IPS signature-match events with severity high or critical.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_idsips_sourcetype> severity IN ("high","critical")
| table _time, source_vm, dest_vm, signature_name, severity, cve
tuning_guidance: Tune out signatures matching known-benign scanning/vulnerability-assessment traffic from authorized tools.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and destination VM roles.
Check the destination VM for signs of successful exploitation (process, file, or network anomalies).
response_guidance: Isolate the destination VM if compromise is confirmed; patch the underlying vulnerability.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1210: Exploitation of Remote Services

author: Threat Detection Library

title: East-West Traffic Between Segments That Should Be Isolated
description: NSX flow data shows traffic between two segments/security groups that, per the intended microsegmentation design, should have no direct communication path — evidence that segmentation was bypassed, misconfigured, or a rule was too permissive.

data_sources.name: NSX Flow Log
data_sources.description: East-west flow records with source/destination segment metadata.

detection_logic: Joins flow records against a segmentation-intent matrix (allowed segment pairs) and flags flows between disallowed pairs.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_flow_sourcetype>
| lookup segmentation_intent_matrix.csv source_segment, dest_segment OUTPUT allowed
| where allowed=0 OR isnull(allowed)
| stats sum(bytes) AS total_bytes count by source_segment, dest_segment, source_ip, dest_ip
tuning_guidance: Requires and depends entirely on a maintained segmentation-intent matrix; highest-value once available, noisy without it.
investigation_steps: Confirm the flow against the microsegmentation design.
Trace which DFW rule permitted this traffic and correlate with NSX-011/NSX-013.
response_guidance: Tighten the permissive rule; investigate both endpoints for compromise.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1210: Exploitation of Remote Services

author: Threat Detection Library

title: NSX Manager Cluster Node Removed or Cluster Degraded
description: An NSX Manager cluster node was removed or the cluster's health degraded below full quorum, threatening the availability and consistency of network and security policy management for the entire NSX domain.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Cluster membership and health-status change events.

detection_logic: Filters cluster membership-change and degraded-health events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("ClusterNodeRemoved","ClusterDegraded")
| table _time, user, node, cluster_status
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences outside planned maintenance windows.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a maintenance ticket.
Assess quorum status and management-plane availability.
response_guidance: Restore the removed node or address the degradation immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.004: Application or System Exploitation

author: Threat Detection Library

title: NSX API Used for Bulk Policy Export
description: The NSX Policy API was used to export a large volume of security-policy configuration (DFW rules, groups, segments) in a short window, which — while a legitimate backup/documentation activity — also matches reconnaissance behavior ahead of a targeted segmentation-bypass attack.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager API Log
data_sources.path: NSX Manager Policy API access log
data_sources.description: API calls to bulk policy-export endpoints with response size.

detection_logic: Filters Policy API calls to export/list endpoints returning unusually large responses, correlated per user.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_api_sourcetype> api_endpoint="*policy/api/v1/infra*" method="GET"
| stats avg(response_size) AS avg_size stdev(response_size) AS stdev_size by api_endpoint
| join api_endpoint [search index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_api_sourcetype> api_endpoint="*policy/api/v1/infra*" method="GET" | table _time, user, api_endpoint, response_size]
| where response_size > (avg_size + 3*stdev_size)
tuning_guidance: Baseline against known backup/IaC service accounts; expect false positives from legitimate Terraform state refreshes.
investigation_steps: Identify the requesting principal and whether it is an expected automation account.
If unexpected, treat as reconnaissance.
response_guidance: Review API token scope; rotate if compromise is suspected.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: response_size > 95th percentile for this endpoint over trailing 30 days

title: NSX Audit Log Forwarding Disabled or Redirected
description: NSX Manager's audit-log forwarding to the central syslog/Operations for Logs target was disabled or redirected to a different destination, which — if the destination change is unauthorized — can be used to silently divert or suppress evidence of subsequent malicious NSX configuration changes.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.path: NSX Manager syslog exporter config log
data_sources.description: Syslog exporter configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters syslog-exporter configuration-change events where the exporter is disabled or the destination changes to an unrecognized target.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="SyslogExporterChanged"
| lookup known_log_destinations.csv new_target OUTPUT is_known
| where status="disabled" OR isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, old_target, new_target, status
tuning_guidance: Maintain a known-log-destination lookup; alert on all disable events unconditionally.
investigation_steps: This event may itself be under-logged if forwarding was already disabled — cross-check with local NSX Manager logs directly.
Treat as a precursor to further undetected tampering.
response_guidance: Re-enable forwarding to the correct destination immediately; audit all NSX changes made while forwarding was disrupted.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: NSX Manager Local Account Password Reset by Non-Admin Workflow
description: A local NSX Manager account's password was reset outside the expected admin self-service or break-glass workflow, which can indicate an attacker resetting credentials to maintain or regain access to the NSX management plane.

data_sources.name: NSX Manager Audit Log
data_sources.description: Password-reset events for local NSX Manager accounts.

detection_logic: Filters password-reset events for local accounts where the reset method does not match the documented break-glass procedure.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype> event="LocalAccountPasswordReset"
| where reset_method!="documented-break-glass"
| table _time, actor, target_account, reset_method
tuning_guidance: Requires a defined break-glass procedure tag in the source event; otherwise alert on all local-account resets given how rarely they should occur once federated identity is in place.
investigation_steps: Confirm the reset was performed by an authorized administrator through the proper channel.
Check for subsequent logins using the reset account.
response_guidance: Reset again through the proper channel and investigate the actor's other activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Data-at-Rest Encryption Disabled
description: vSAN Data-at-Rest Encryption was disabled on a cluster, which triggers a full re-format/decrypt of all disk groups and removes protection against physical-media theft or improper disk disposal — treat as Critical per KMS-related guidance.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: vSAN encryption configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters vSAN encryption configuration-change events where the new state is disabled.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vsan.encryption.changed"
| where new_state="disabled"
| table _time, user, cluster, old_state, new_state
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; disabling encryption on a live cluster is an extremely rare, deliberate action.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Determine whether decryption has begun and halt if unauthorized.
response_guidance: Re-enable immediately and audit who requested the change and why.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact

author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN KMS Cluster Configuration Changed
description: The Key Management Server cluster backing vSAN encryption was changed, added, or removed on the vCenter trust relationship — if pointed at an attacker-controlled KMS or an unreachable one, this can be used to stage a key-unavailability denial-of-service or key-exfiltration attack against every encrypted vSAN datastore.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: KMS cluster configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters KMS cluster configuration-change events (add/remove/modify trust).
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vc.kms.ClusterChanged"
| table _time, user, kms_cluster, change_type
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the rarity and criticality of KMS trust changes.
investigation_steps: Verify the KMS cluster/endpoint is the expected, authorized one.
Confirm certificate trust was established through the proper process.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized KMS trust changes immediately; this is a Critical-tier response per KMS-change guidance.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact

author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Encryption Rekey Operation Initiated Outside Schedule
description: A vSAN encryption rekey (shallow or deep) was manually initiated outside the documented rotation schedule; while rekeying is a normal maintenance operation, an unscheduled deep rekey can also be used to mask key-compromise cleanup or to induce cluster-wide I/O load as a denial-of-service.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: vSAN rekey operation start events.

detection_logic: Filters rekey-start events outside a scheduled-maintenance lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vsan.rekey.started"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user, cluster, rekey_type
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintenance-window lookup; deep rekeys naturally occur after suspected key compromise so correlate with recent KMS changes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for a preceding suspected-compromise event that would explain an unscheduled deep rekey.
response_guidance: No action needed if authorized; investigate KMS/credential state if not.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact

author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Disk Group Removed or Unmounted
description: A vSAN disk group was removed or force-unmounted, which reduces cluster storage capacity/resiliency and — if performed against multiple hosts — can be an early step in a destructive attack against the vSAN datastore.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: Disk group removal/unmount events.

detection_logic: Filters disk-group removal and forced-unmount events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type IN ("com.vmware.vsan.diskgroup.removed","com.vmware.vsan.diskgroup.unmounted")
| table _time, user, host, disk_group
tuning_guidance: Correlate with planned hardware-maintenance tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check for concurrent removals across multiple hosts (VSAN-005).
response_guidance: Escalate immediately if unauthorized and part of a broader pattern.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass vSAN Disk Group Removal Across Cluster
description: Disk groups were removed or unmounted across multiple hosts in the same vSAN cluster within a short window, consistent with a coordinated destructive attack against the shared datastore rather than routine single-host hardware maintenance.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: Disk group removal/unmount events aggregated per cluster per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct hosts with disk-group removal/unmount events within the same cluster within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type IN ("com.vmware.vsan.diskgroup.removed","com.vmware.vsan.diskgroup.unmounted")
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats dc(host) AS host_count values(host) AS hosts by _time, cluster
| where host_count>=3
tuning_guidance: Suppress during confirmed hardware-refresh maintenance windows.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live ransomware/destructive-attack indicator absent an explicit maintenance ticket.
Halt further removals and assess data availability.
response_guidance: Engage incident response immediately; this pattern mirrors the ransomware kill-chain's storage-manipulation stage.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Storage Policy Weakened Reducing Fault Tolerance
description: A vSAN storage policy (SPBM) was modified to reduce the Failures To Tolerate (FTT) level or otherwise weaken redundancy for VMs assigned to it, reducing resiliency against subsequent disk-group or host loss.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: Storage policy modification events with FTT before/after values.

detection_logic: Filters storage-policy modification events where the new FTT value is lower than the old value.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.pbm.profile.updated"
| where new_ftt<old_ftt
| table _time, user, policy_name, old_ftt, new_ftt
tuning_guidance: Confirm against capacity-planning change tickets.
investigation_steps: Determine how many VMs are assigned to the weakened policy.
Assess resulting resiliency exposure.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Cluster Removed from vCenter Inventory or Un-Clustered
description: A vSAN-enabled cluster's hosts were removed from the cluster or vSAN was disabled at the cluster level, an operation that can render the shared datastore inaccessible to every VM depending on it.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: Cluster vSAN-enablement and host-removal events.

detection_logic: Filters vSAN cluster-disable and mass host-removal-from-cluster events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type IN ("com.vmware.vsan.cluster.disabled","com.vmware.vc.ClusterRemoveHostEvent")
| table _time, user, cluster, action
tuning_guidance: Alert on all vsan.cluster.disabled events; correlate host-removal events with decommission tickets.
investigation_steps: Treat vSAN-disable as a live incident.
Confirm host removals against a decommission plan.
response_guidance: Re-enable/restore immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN File Service Domain Deleted
description: A vSAN File Service domain (and its associated file shares) was deleted, potentially destroying shared file-based data used by dependent workloads.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: vSAN File Service domain deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters File Service domain-deletion events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vsan.fileservice.domain.deleted"
| table _time, user, file_service_domain
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; domain deletion is rare and destructive.
investigation_steps: Confirm the deletion was authorized and data was backed up beforehand.
Determine what shares/workloads depended on this domain.
response_guidance: Restore from backup if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN iSCSI Target Created or Access Control Widened
description: A vSAN iSCSI target was created, or an existing target's initiator group access control was widened, potentially exposing block storage to hosts outside the intended consumer set.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: vSAN iSCSI target and initiator-group configuration events.

detection_logic: Filters iSCSI target-creation and initiator-group-widening events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type IN ("com.vmware.vsan.iscsi.target.created","com.vmware.vsan.iscsi.initiatorgroup.changed")
| table _time, user, target_name, change_type
tuning_guidance: Confirm against storage-provisioning change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new/widened access is intentional.
Check what data resides on the target LUN.
response_guidance: Restrict access if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Health Service Alarm Silenced or Disabled
description: A vSAN Health Service check or its associated alarm was disabled or silenced, which can be used to mask an ongoing storage-availability or security-configuration issue (including the very conditions this catalogue's other vSAN detections depend on being alarmed).

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: vSAN Health Service check disable/silence events.

detection_logic: Filters Health Service check disable/silence events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vsan.health.check.disabled"
| table _time, user, health_check, action
tuning_guidance: Some health checks are legitimately disabled in specific supported configurations (e.g. stretched cluster witness checks); maintain an allow-list.
investigation_steps: Confirm the disabled check against the allow-list of known-supported exceptions.
If not listed, investigate why visibility into this check was removed.
response_guidance: Re-enable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Stretched Cluster Witness Host Changed
description: The witness host/appliance for a vSAN stretched cluster was changed or removed, which can compromise the cluster's ability to resolve split-brain scenarios and maintain quorum during a site failure.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: Stretched-cluster witness configuration events.

detection_logic: Filters witness-host configuration-change events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vsan.stretchedcluster.witness.changed"
| table _time, user, cluster, old_witness, new_witness
tuning_guidance: Confirm against DR/site-topology change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new witness is the expected, authorized appliance.
Assess quorum/failover readiness.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: vSAN Performance Service Data Export or API Enumeration at Scale
description: The vSAN Performance Service API was used to enumerate metrics/objects across an unusually large number of clusters or objects in a short window by a single principal, consistent with infrastructure-discovery reconnaissance ahead of a targeted attack.

data_sources.name: vCenter API Log
data_sources.description: vSAN Performance Service API call volume per principal.

detection_logic: Counts distinct objects queried via the Performance Service API per principal within a rolling window and flags high-volume enumeration.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_api_sourcetype> api_endpoint="*vsan/performance*"
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats dc(object_id) AS object_count by _time, user
| where object_count>=100
tuning_guidance: Baseline against known monitoring-tool service accounts (vROps, third-party monitoring) to reduce noise significantly.
investigation_steps: Identify the requesting principal.
If not a known monitoring integration, investigate for reconnaissance activity.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; correlate with other discovery-phase indicators.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1082: System Information Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Admin Login Failure Threshold Exceeded
description: Repeated failed logins against a VCF Operations administrative account exceeded the threshold, consistent with password-guessing against the monitoring/analytics plane, which itself has broad read access across the SDDC.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Authentication failure events with source IP and account.

detection_logic: Counts failed authentication events per user within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="AuthenticationFailed"
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count by _time, user, src_ip
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known monitoring-integration accounts with expected periodic auth retries.
investigation_steps: Identify source IP.
Check for a subsequent successful login (OPS-002).
response_guidance: Lock the account if attack is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Successful Login After Failure Burst
description: A VCF Operations account authenticated successfully immediately following a burst of failed login attempts, the classic successful-brute-force pattern against the operations/monitoring plane.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Sequenced authentication failure and success events for the same account.

detection_logic: Correlates a failure burst (>=5 in 10m) followed by a success event for the same account within 5 minutes.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="AuthenticationFailed"
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count AS fail_count by _time, user
| where fail_count>=5
| join user [search index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="AuthenticationSuccess" | table _time, user, src_ip]
| where _time_success>_time AND (_time_success-_time)<=300
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive pattern; investigate all matches.
investigation_steps: Identify all dashboards/data accessed during the resulting session.
Reset credentials and review MFA enrollment.
response_guidance: Force password reset and session termination.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Alert Definition Disabled or Deleted at Scale
description: A large number of VCF Operations alert definitions were disabled or deleted in a short window, which can blind the operations/security team to subsequent malicious activity or ongoing outages across the monitored SDDC.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Alert definition disable/delete events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts alert-definition disable/delete events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("AlertDefinitionDisabled","AlertDefinitionDeleted")
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(alert_definition) AS definitions by _time, user
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Correlate with monitoring-platform migration/tuning projects.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident absent a known tuning project.
Determine which alerts were disabled and whether that correlates with other suspicious activity.
response_guidance: Re-enable the alerts immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Notification/Webhook Endpoint Changed
description: An outbound notification or webhook endpoint used by VCF Operations to send alerts was changed to an unrecognized destination, which can silently redirect security/operational alerts away from the legitimate SOC/ITSM integration, or exfiltrate alert content (which itself often contains sensitive infrastructure detail) to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Notification/webhook endpoint configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters notification-endpoint change events where the new endpoint does not match a known-destination lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="NotificationEndpointChanged"
| lookup known_notification_endpoints.csv new_endpoint OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, old_endpoint, new_endpoint
tuning_guidance: Maintain a known-endpoint lookup; alert on all unrecognized destinations.
investigation_steps: Verify the new endpoint belongs to an authorized integration.
Check whether alerts stopped reaching the legitimate SOC/ITSM tool afterward.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized and audit alert delivery gaps.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Custom Group/Application Membership Manipulated at Scale
description: An unusually large number of objects were added to or removed from a custom group/application definition in a short window, which can be used to move monitored objects out of scope for alert policies or compliance dashboards tied to that grouping.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Group-membership change events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts group-membership change events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="GroupMembershipChanged"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count by _time, user, group_name
| where count>=20
tuning_guidance: Baseline against known bulk-tagging automation.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Check whether any alert policies scoped to this group are affected.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Data Collector/Adapter Removed
description: A management pack adapter or data collector instance feeding VCF Operations (e.g. the vCenter or NSX adapter) was removed or disabled, cutting off monitoring visibility into that platform.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Adapter instance removal/disable events.

detection_logic: Filters adapter removal/disable events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("AdapterInstanceRemoved","AdapterInstanceDisabled")
| table _time, user, adapter_type, adapter_instance
tuning_guidance: Correlate with decommission tickets for retired infrastructure.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Determine what visibility gap results and for how long.
response_guidance: Restore if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Policy Applied That Suppresses Critical Alerts
description: An alert/monitoring policy was applied to an object or object group that suppresses critical-severity alerts, effectively silencing detection for the scoped infrastructure without disabling the underlying alert definitions.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Policy assignment events with alert-suppression settings.

detection_logic: Filters policy-assignment events where the applied policy suppresses critical alerts.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="PolicyApplied" suppresses_critical=true
| table _time, user, policy_name, scope
tuning_guidance: Some legitimate maintenance-mode policies suppress alerts temporarily; correlate with maintenance windows.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and time-bound scope.
Determine what critical conditions occurred while suppressed.
response_guidance: Remove the policy if unauthorized or left in place beyond the maintenance window.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations API Token Created with Administrative Scope
description: An API token/service account credential was created for VCF Operations with administrative-level scope, which — combined with the platform's broad read access across the SDDC and its ability to trigger remediation actions — represents a high-value persistence target if leaked.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: API token creation events with scope/role.

detection_logic: Filters token-creation events where the assigned scope/role is administrative.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="ApiTokenCreated"
| where scope="admin"
| table _time, user, token_id, scope
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a change ticket for legitimate automation onboarding.
investigation_steps: Verify the requester and intended use case.
Confirm the token is stored in an approved secrets manager, not embedded in code.
response_guidance: Revoke if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Remediation Action Triggered Against Unusual Scope
description: A VCF Operations automated remediation action (e.g. power-off, VM reclamation, resource reconfiguration) was triggered against an unusually large scope of objects, which — if the remediation logic or trigger condition was tampered with — can be abused to cause a fleet-wide service disruption through the operations platform's own legitimate automation capability.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Remediation action execution events with target object count.

detection_logic: Filters remediation-action execution events where the affected object count exceeds a baseline threshold.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="RemediationActionExecuted"
| where object_count>=20
| table _time, user, action_name, object_count
tuning_guidance: Baseline per action type; some remediations (e.g. snapshot cleanup) legitimately touch many objects.
investigation_steps: Confirm the action's trigger condition/policy was not tampered with.
Assess resulting service impact.
response_guidance: Halt further automated remediation execution if malicious tampering is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations Super Admin Role Granted
description: A user was granted the VCF Operations Super Admin (or equivalent top-level) role, which grants full control over monitoring, alerting, automation, and — via integrated remediation actions — indirect control over the monitored SDDC infrastructure itself.

data_sources.name: VCF Operations Audit Log
data_sources.description: Role-assignment events with role name.

detection_logic: Filters role-assignment events where the granted role is a top-level administrative role.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<ops_audit_sourcetype> event="RoleAssigned" role="SuperAdmin"
| table _time, actor, target_user, role
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; correlate with change-management approval.
investigation_steps: Confirm the grant against an approved access request.
Review the target account's subsequent activity.
response_guidance: Revoke if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Ingestion Pipeline Stopped
description: A log-ingestion pipeline/agent feeding VCF Operations for Logs stopped receiving events from one or more sources, which — whether from a configuration change or a targeted stop — creates a detection blind spot across every other detection in this library that depends on that log source.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs system logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight System Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs system health log
data_sources.description: Ingestion-rate anomaly and pipeline-stopped events per source.

detection_logic: Flags sources with zero ingested events over an expected-interval window, based on historical ingestion baseline.
spl:
| metadata type=sourcetypes index=<vcf_index>
| where recentTime < relative_time(now(), "-30m")
| table sourcetype, recentTime
tuning_guidance: Exclude known low-volume/intermittent sources; tune the multiplier per source criticality.
investigation_steps: Determine if the source host/agent is down vs. deliberately reconfigured.
Check for a preceding configuration-change event for the affected forwarder/agent.
response_guidance: Restore ingestion immediately; this is a Priority-1 visibility gap.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: no events received for 3x the source's typical inter-event interval

title: VCF Operations for Logs Retention Policy Shortened
description: The log-retention policy was shortened, which can be used to accelerate the deletion of evidence of prior malicious activity across the entire SDDC's centralized logging.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs retention config log
data_sources.description: Retention-policy configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters retention-policy change events where the new retention period is shorter than the old one.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="RetentionPolicyChanged"
| where new_retention_days<old_retention_days
| table _time, user, old_retention_days, new_retention_days
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; retention shortening is rare and directly impacts forensic capability.
investigation_steps: Confirm business/compliance justification.
If unauthorized, treat as active anti-forensics and preserve any existing exports/backups immediately.
response_guidance: Revert immediately and export logs before the shortened window takes effect.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Alert Query Modified or Deleted
description: A saved alert query in VCF Operations for Logs was modified in a way that narrows its matching scope, or was deleted outright, silently reducing detection coverage.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs alert config log
data_sources.description: Alert query modification/deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters alert-query modification/deletion events for manual triage.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("AlertQueryModified","AlertQueryDeleted")
| table _time, user, alert_name, action
tuning_guidance: Correlate against known tuning projects; ideally diff the query text before/after for narrowing detection.
investigation_steps: Review the query diff for scope narrowing.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Restore if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Forwarding to External SIEM Disabled
description: Log forwarding from VCF Operations for Logs to an external SIEM was disabled, which — if this catalogue's detections run in that downstream SIEM — can blind every detection in this entire library simultaneously.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs forwarder config log
data_sources.description: Forwarding destination disable/removal events.

detection_logic: Filters forwarder-configuration events where an external SIEM destination is disabled or removed.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="ForwarderChanged" status="disabled"
| table _time, user, destination, status
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the catastrophic detection-coverage impact.
investigation_steps: This is a self-referential blind spot — if this alert itself is generated downstream of the disabled forwarder, it will not fire; rely on the local VCF Operations for Logs system logs directly, or a heartbeat detection in the downstream SIEM (LOGS-001-style) as backstop.
Treat as a top-priority incident.
response_guidance: Re-enable immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Local Admin Account Used Instead of Federated Identity
description: The local built-in administrator account for VCF Operations for Logs authenticated in an environment where federated identity (SSO/LDAP) is the expected access path, which can indicate use of a persistence account or a fallback used to bypass conditional-access/MFA policy enforced only at the identity provider.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs authentication log
data_sources.description: Authentication events flagged with auth_type=local.

detection_logic: Filters successful authentication events where auth_type is local rather than federated.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="AuthenticationSuccess" auth_type="local"
| table _time, user, auth_type, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Exclude documented break-glass procedures; otherwise alert on all local-account use once federation is enforced.
investigation_steps: Confirm this was an authorized break-glass access.
If not, treat the local admin credential as potentially compromised.
response_guidance: Rotate the local admin credential if unauthorized use is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Content Pack Removed
description: A content pack (bundling dashboards, alerts, and parsers for a given product, e.g. the NSX or vSAN content pack) was removed, silently disabling the parsing and alerting logic it provided for that product's log stream.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs content pack log
data_sources.description: Content pack removal events.

detection_logic: Filters content pack-removal events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="ContentPackRemoved"
| table _time, user, content_pack
tuning_guidance: Correlate with intentional platform-cleanup projects.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Determine which alerts/parsers depended on this content pack.
response_guidance: Reinstall if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Query Used to Search for Credential Strings
description: A user ran interactive log searches using terms consistent with hunting for embedded credentials (e.g. 'password', 'apikey', 'secret', 'token') across the centralized log corpus, which — since logs frequently contain accidentally-logged secrets — represents a credential-harvesting technique against the logging platform itself.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs search-query log
data_sources.description: Interactive search query text per user.

detection_logic: Filters interactive search-query events where the query text matches a credential-hunting keyword pattern.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="SearchExecuted"
| where match(query_text, "(?i)(password|apikey|api_key|secret|token|credential)")
| table _time, user, query_text
tuning_guidance: Exclude known security/IR team accounts performing legitimate credential-exposure hunts; scope this detection to non-security accounts.
investigation_steps: Determine whether the user has a legitimate reason for this search (security team, incident response).
If not, treat as credential-harvesting reconnaissance.
response_guidance: Investigate the user's broader activity; rotate any credentials the search may have surfaced.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Cluster Node Removed or Ingestion Capacity Reduced
description: A VCF Operations for Logs cluster node was removed, reducing ingestion capacity and potentially causing event drops under load — a subtler variant of the forwarding-disabled attack that degrades rather than eliminates visibility.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs cluster config log
data_sources.description: Cluster node removal events.

detection_logic: Filters cluster node-removal events outside maintenance windows.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="ClusterNodeRemoved"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user, node
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintenance-window lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a maintenance ticket.
Monitor for subsequent event-drop/queue-backpressure alarms.
response_guidance: Restore capacity if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499.004: Application or System Exploitation

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Operations for Logs Bulk Export of Historical Logs
description: A user exported an unusually large volume of historical log data in a short window, which — while a legitimate forensic or compliance activity — can also be used to exfiltrate the full sensitive-infrastructure telemetry stored in the centralized logging platform.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs export log
data_sources.description: Log export events with row/byte count.

detection_logic: Filters export events exceeding a byte/row-count threshold.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="LogsExported"
| eventstats avg(export_size) AS avg_size stdev(export_size) AS stdev_size by user
| where export_size > (avg_size + 3*stdev_size)
| table _time, user, export_size, query_scope
tuning_guidance: Exclude known compliance/backup export jobs.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the export.
Determine the destination of the exported data.
response_guidance: Investigate for exfiltration if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1213: Data from Information Repositories

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: export_size exceeds 95th percentile for this user over trailing 30 days

title: VCF Operations for Logs Parser/Extraction Rule Tampered to Drop Fields
description: A custom field-extraction/parser rule was modified in a way that stops extracting a security-relevant field (e.g. user, source IP), which can silently break every downstream alert query that filters or groups on that field without deleting the alert itself.
required_log_source: VCF Operations for Logs audit logs

data_sources.name: Log Insight Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Operations for Logs parser config log
data_sources.description: Field-extraction rule modification events.

detection_logic: Lists field-extraction rule modification events for manual review against known security-relevant field names.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<logs_audit_sourcetype> event="ExtractionRuleModified"
| table _time, user, extraction_rule, field_name
tuning_guidance: Requires manual review since automated detection of 'stops extracting' needs a before/after schema diff not always available in the audit event; treat as a hunting query pending richer telemetry.
investigation_steps: Diff the extraction rule before and after the change.
Test whether dependent alert queries still populate the affected field.
response_guidance: Restore the original extraction logic if the change was unauthorized or unintentional.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Service Account Credential Modified
description: A cloud/endpoint credential stored in VCF Automation (used by the automation platform to provision and manage infrastructure) was modified, which can allow an attacker to redirect provisioning actions or capture the credential for use outside the platform.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Credential modification events.

detection_logic: Filters credential-modification events in the Automation credential store.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="CredentialModified"
| table _time, user, credential_name, credential_type
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate credential rotation.
investigation_steps: Confirm the modification was performed by the credential owner/authorized admin.
Review what provisioning actions ran using this credential afterward.
response_guidance: Rotate the credential if unauthorized modification is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Blueprint/Template Modified by Non-Owner
description: A deployment blueprint/template was modified by a user other than its designated owner or an approved reviewer, which — since blueprints define what infrastructure and configuration gets deployed — is a software supply-chain manipulation point: a tampered blueprint can inject backdoored configuration into every subsequent deployment made from it.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Blueprint modification events with owner/actor comparison.

detection_logic: Filters blueprint-modification events where the acting user does not match the blueprint's designated owner/reviewer group.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="BlueprintModified"
| where actor!=owner
| table _time, actor, blueprint_name, owner
tuning_guidance: Requires an owner/reviewer-group lookup per blueprint; platform teams using shared service accounts will need that account added to each owner group.
investigation_steps: Diff the blueprint content before/after for injected commands, scripts, or configuration.
Determine every deployment made from this blueprint since the modification.
response_guidance: Revert the blueprint and redeploy/patch any workloads provisioned from the tampered version.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Workflow Contains Suspicious Script Action
description: An orchestration workflow (vRO-based) was created or modified to include a scriptable-task action invoking shell/PowerShell execution or an outbound network call to an unrecognized host, which can be used to embed arbitrary code execution into routine automation runs.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Workflow modification events with script-action content.

detection_logic: Filters workflow-modification events where script-action content matches shell/process-execution or unrecognized-outbound-host patterns.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="WorkflowModified"
| where match(script_content, "(?i)(cmd\.exe|powershell|/bin/sh|curl |wget |Invoke-WebRequest)")
| table _time, user, workflow_name, script_content
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate given legitimate automation scripting; scope to workflows outside the platform-team's known automation catalog.
investigation_steps: Review the full script content for malicious intent.
Determine what triggers this workflow and how frequently it runs.
response_guidance: Disable the workflow pending review if malicious intent is suspected.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Mass Deployment Request in Short Window
description: An unusually large number of deployment requests were submitted by a single user or API principal in a short window, consistent with the automation-compromise attack chain: a compromised Automation credential used to rapidly provision a large number of workloads — e.g. for cryptomining, botnet infrastructure, or resource-exhaustion denial-of-service against the underlying VCF capacity.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Deployment request events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts deployment-request events per actor within a rolling window and flags counts above a threshold.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="DeploymentRequested"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(blueprint_name) AS blueprints by _time, actor
| where count>=15
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known bulk-provisioning automation/CI-CD pipelines.
investigation_steps: Identify whether the actor is a known automation pipeline.
If not, treat as the automation-compromise attack chain and investigate the credential/API-token used.
response_guidance: Suspend the actor's provisioning rights and destroy unauthorized deployments.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Deployment Destroy/Delete at Scale
description: An unusually large number of deployments were destroyed/deleted by a single actor in a short window, consistent with a destructive attack against automation-managed infrastructure carried out through the automation platform's own legitimate teardown capability.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Deployment destroy/delete events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts deployment destroy/delete events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("DeploymentDestroyed","DeploymentDeleted")
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(deployment_name) AS deployments by _time, actor
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known IaC pipeline teardown jobs (e.g. ephemeral environment cleanup).
investigation_steps: Confirm against a decommission plan.
Treat as a live ransomware/destructive-attack indicator absent one.
response_guidance: Suspend the actor and halt further destructions immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Cloud Zone/Endpoint Added Pointing Outside Managed Environment
description: A new cloud account/endpoint or cloud zone was added to VCF Automation pointing to infrastructure outside the organization's known-managed vCenter/cloud accounts, which could be used to provision attacker-controlled infrastructure using organizational automation credentials.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Automation cloud account config log
data_sources.description: Cloud account/endpoint creation events.

detection_logic: Filters cloud-account creation events where the target endpoint does not match a known-managed-infrastructure lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="CloudAccountCreated"
| lookup known_managed_endpoints.csv endpoint_target OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, endpoint_name, endpoint_target
tuning_guidance: Maintain a known-endpoint lookup; multi-cloud environments will need this actively curated.
investigation_steps: Verify the endpoint is an authorized, newly-onboarded environment.
If not, treat as attacker-controlled infrastructure setup.
response_guidance: Remove the endpoint immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Custom Resource/ABX Action with Outbound Network Call Added
description: An Action-Based Extensibility (ABX) action or custom resource script was created/modified containing an outbound HTTP call to a host outside a known-allowlist, which — since ABX actions run with the platform's provisioning credentials in response to lifecycle events — represents a high-value C2/exfiltration channel embedded in routine automation.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Automation ABX action version-control log
data_sources.description: ABX action creation/modification events with script content.

detection_logic: Filters ABX action creation/modification events where script content includes outbound HTTP calls to hosts not on an allowlist.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("AbxActionCreated","AbxActionModified")
| rex field=script_content "https?://(?<target_host>[a-zA-Z0-9\.\-]+)"
| lookup allowed_outbound_hosts.csv target_host OUTPUT is_allowed
| where isnull(is_allowed)
| table _time, user, action_name, target_host
tuning_guidance: Maintain an allowlist of legitimate external integration endpoints (ITSM, notification services).
investigation_steps: Review the full action script and confirm the destination host's legitimacy.
Check the action's trigger conditions to assess exposure/frequency.
response_guidance: Disable the action immediately if the destination is unrecognized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1071: Application Layer Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Approval Policy Bypassed or Removed
description: An approval policy requiring manager/security sign-off before deployment was removed from a project/blueprint, or a deployment was pushed through with an approval status of bypassed, undermining the governance control meant to catch AUTO-004/AUTO-005-style mass-provisioning abuse before it happens.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Approval-policy removal and approval-bypass events.

detection_logic: Filters approval-policy removal events and deployment events with an approval_status of bypassed.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("ApprovalPolicyRemoved","DeploymentApprovalBypassed")
| table _time, user, project_name, policy_action
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; approval bypass is a governance-control failure regardless of intent.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the policy removal/bypass.
Review what deployments proceeded without the approval gate.
response_guidance: Restore the policy immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1548: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Project Membership Escalation
description: A user was added to a project with an administrator role, or an existing member's role was escalated from member to administrator, granting broader provisioning and governance-policy control within that project scope.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Project role-assignment events.

detection_logic: Filters project role-assignment events where the new role is administrator.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="ProjectRoleAssigned" role="administrator"
| table _time, actor, target_user, project_name, role
tuning_guidance: Confirm against access-request tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
Review the target user's subsequent activity in this project.
response_guidance: Revoke if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Git Integration Repository Changed
description: The Git repository backing VCF Automation's blueprint version control was changed to a different URL, which — if pointed at an attacker-controlled repository — allows the attacker to fully control the content of every blueprint synced from that source going forward.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Automation Git integration config log
data_sources.description: Git integration repository-URL change events.

detection_logic: Filters Git integration configuration-change events on the repository URL field.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="GitIntegrationChanged"
| table _time, user, old_repo_url, new_repo_url
