tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the supply-chain severity.
investigation_steps: Verify the new repository URL is the authorized organizational source.
Audit blueprint content synced since the change.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized and re-sync from the trusted repository.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation API Token Used from Unrecognized Source Address
description: A VCF Automation API token/refresh token was used from a source IP address inconsistent with the token's expected CI/CD or automation-host origin, suggesting the token was exfiltrated and is being used by an attacker.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation API Log
data_sources.description: API calls with token ID and source IP, joined against a known-source lookup per token.

detection_logic: Joins API call events against a per-token expected-source lookup and flags mismatches.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_api_sourcetype>
| lookup token_expected_sources.csv token_id OUTPUT expected_src_ip
| where src_ip!=expected_src_ip
| table _time, token_id, src_ip, expected_src_ip, api_endpoint
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-token expected-source lookup; high value for CI/CD tokens with static origins.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether the source IP is a legitimate new CI/CD runner or VPN egress point.
If not, treat the token as compromised.
response_guidance: Revoke and reissue the token immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Day-2 Action Executed Against High-Value Deployment
description: A custom day-2 action (a post-provisioning operational action, potentially running arbitrary scripts) was executed against a deployment tagged as high-value/production, warranting review given the platform's broad execution reach into deployed workloads.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.path: VCF Automation day-2 action execution log
data_sources.description: Day-2 action execution events joined against a high-value deployment tag lookup.

detection_logic: Joins day-2 action execution events against a high-value-deployment tag lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="Day2ActionExecuted"
| lookup high_value_deployments.csv deployment_name OUTPUT is_high_value
| where is_high_value=1
| table _time, user, deployment_name, action_name
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained high-value-deployment tag; standalone low-value without it.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the action.
Review the action's script content if unfamiliar.
response_guidance: Low urgency standalone; escalate if action content is unrecognized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Extensibility Subscription Bound to Suspicious Action
description: An extensibility subscription was created binding a lifecycle event (e.g. every deployment-complete event) to a custom ABX action, which — if the bound action is malicious — creates a persistence mechanism that automatically re-executes attacker code on every future occurrence of that platform-wide event.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Extensibility subscription creation events with bound event type and action.

detection_logic: Filters subscription-creation events bound to broad/frequent lifecycle event topics for review.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="SubscriptionCreated"
| where event_topic IN ("compute.provision.post","deployment.complete")
| table _time, user, event_topic, bound_action
tuning_guidance: Review each new subscription binding against the change catalog; broad event topics warrant closer scrutiny.
investigation_steps: Review the bound action's content and origin (correlate with AUTO-003/AUTO-007).
Determine how many future events this subscription will trigger against.
response_guidance: Remove the subscription if the bound action is malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1546: Event Triggered Execution

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Catalog Item Published Bypassing Content Sharing Policy
description: A catalog item was shared/published to a broader project scope than the content-sharing policy permits, potentially exposing a tampered blueprint or template to a wider set of consumers than intended.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.description: Catalog item sharing-scope change events.

detection_logic: Filters catalog-sharing events where the new scope exceeds the item's declared sharing policy.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype> event="CatalogItemShared"
| lookup catalog_sharing_policy.csv catalog_item OUTPUT allowed_scope
| where new_scope!=allowed_scope
| table _time, user, catalog_item, new_scope, allowed_scope
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-item sharing-policy lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the broader sharing scope.
Review the catalog item's content for tampering.
response_guidance: Restrict the scope if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: VCF Automation Compromise-to-Fleet-Impact Correlation
description: The named automation-compromise attack chain: an Automation credential or project-membership modification (AUTO-001/AUTO-009), followed by a workflow/blueprint/template change (AUTO-002/AUTO-003), followed by mass deployment execution (AUTO-004), affecting a large number of workloads within a short overall window — this sequence is the highest-confidence signal that the automation platform itself has been weaponized against the fleet it manages.

data_sources.name: VCF Automation Audit Log
data_sources.path: Correlated credential/project, blueprint/workflow, and deployment events for the same actor.
data_sources.description: Multi-stage correlation across AUTO-001/AUTO-009, AUTO-002/AUTO-003, and AUTO-004.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) a credential or project-role event, (2) a blueprint/workflow modification, (3) a mass-deployment event — all for the same actor within a 60-minute window, in that order.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<auto_audit_sourcetype>
| eval stage=case(event IN ("CredentialModified","ProjectRoleAssigned"), "1_credential", event IN ("BlueprintModified","WorkflowModified"), "2_content", event="DeploymentRequested", "3_deploy")
| where isnotnull(stage)
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by actor
| where stage_count>=3 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=3600
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support (Splunk Enterprise Security or equivalent); this is the flagship chain for VCF Automation and should be a Tier-1 alert.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed incident.
Immediately suspend the actor's credentials and API tokens.
Enumerate every deployment created during stage 3 and quarantine/destroy unauthorized ones.
response_guidance: Full incident response: credential rotation, deployment audit, blueprint/workflow content review, and root-cause analysis of the initial credential compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Master Authentication Failure Threshold Exceeded
description: Repeated failed authentication attempts against the Salt Master's API/console exceeded the threshold, consistent with password-guessing against the master node that controls every minion in the fleet.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.path: /var/log/salt/master (or VCF Salt Config API audit log)
data_sources.description: Authentication failure events.

detection_logic: Counts failed authentication events against the Salt Master API within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="AuthenticationFailed"
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count by _time, user, src_ip
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Exclude known automation/CI accounts with expected retry behavior.
investigation_steps: Identify source IP.
Check for a subsequent successful authentication (SALT-002).
response_guidance: Lock the account and block the source IP if attack is confirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Master Successful Login After Failure Burst
description: A successful authentication to the Salt Master immediately followed a burst of failed attempts — since a compromised Salt Master grants control over every minion in the fleet, this is one of the highest-impact successful-brute-force patterns in the entire VCF stack.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Sequenced authentication failure and success events.

detection_logic: Correlates a failure burst followed by a success event for the same account within 5 minutes.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="AuthenticationFailed"
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats count AS fail_count by _time, user
| where fail_count>=5
| join user [search index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="AuthenticationSuccess" | table _time, user, src_ip]
| where _time_success>_time AND (_time_success-_time)<=300
tuning_guidance: Low false-positive pattern; investigate all matches as a top-priority incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed fleet-wide compromise risk.
Immediately review all subsequent Salt state applications and command executions from this session.
response_guidance: Rotate Salt Master credentials/keys and audit all minion activity since the login.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Minion Key Accepted Without Prior Pending Request Review
description: A minion key was accepted on the Salt Master, admitting a new node into the trust relationship that allows the master to execute arbitrary commands on it — and, via minion-side command return channels, allows a rogue minion to potentially return falsified data. Unauthorized key acceptance can also indicate an attacker legitimizing a rogue minion they control.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Minion key acceptance events.

detection_logic: Filters key-acceptance events joined against a known/expected-minion inventory lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="KeyAccepted"
| lookup expected_minion_inventory.csv minion_id OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, user, minion_id, key_fingerprint
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained expected-minion inventory; high value in fleets provisioned via a controlled IaC process.
investigation_steps: Verify the minion_id corresponds to a legitimately provisioned host.
Check the key fingerprint against the host's actual generated key out-of-band if possible.
response_guidance: Reject/delete the key immediately if the minion is not recognized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Minion Key Auto-Accept Enabled
description: The Salt Master's auto_accept configuration was enabled, causing every new minion key to be trusted automatically without administrative review — this removes the primary control preventing a rogue/attacker-controlled minion from joining the trust relationship.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Master configuration-change events for the auto_accept setting.

detection_logic: Filters master configuration-change events where auto_accept is set to true.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="MasterConfigChanged" setting="auto_accept" new_value="true"
| table _time, user, setting, new_value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; auto_accept should never be enabled in a production Salt Master.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Review all keys accepted while auto_accept was enabled.
response_guidance: Disable immediately and review/re-validate every minion key accepted during the exposure window.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Remote Execution Command Targeting Wildcard/All Minions
description: A Salt remote-execution command (salt '*' ...) was run targeting all minions or a broad wildcard glob, which — combined with an arbitrary shell/cmd module — is the core mechanism of the Salt-compromise attack chain: fleet-wide command execution from a single compromised master session.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Job execution events with target glob and function name.

detection_logic: Filters job-execution events where the target matches a wildcard/broad glob pattern and the function is a command-execution module.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="JobExecuted"
| where (target="*" OR match(target, "^\*")) AND match(function, "(cmd\.run|cmd\.exec_code|cmd\.script)")
| table _time, user, target, function, job_id
tuning_guidance: Some legitimate fleet-wide state applications use wildcard targets; scope this detection to the cmd.* execution modules specifically rather than state.apply, which carries far higher risk when combined with a broad target.
investigation_steps: Retrieve the full command/script executed via the job_id.
Determine what minions returned results and what those results contain.
response_guidance: Treat as a fleet-wide incident; isolate affected minions and investigate the command's effect on each.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt State Applied Fleet-Wide Outside Change Window
description: A state.apply/state.highstate run was executed against a broad minion target outside a declared change window, which can push a tampered state definition (SALT-007) to the entire fleet under the guise of routine configuration management.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: State-application job events joined against a maintenance-window lookup.

detection_logic: Filters state.apply/state.highstate job events with broad targets outside maintenance windows.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="JobExecuted" function IN ("state.apply","state.highstate")
| where match(target, "^\*") OR match(target, "@")
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user, target, function
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintenance-window lookup; scheduled/automated state applications are routine and expected within the window.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Diff the applied state's content against the version-controlled source (correlate with SALT-007).
response_guidance: Roll back if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt State File / Pillar Data Modified Outside Version Control Workflow
description: A Salt state (.sls) file or pillar data file was modified directly rather than through the SaltStack Config version-controlled pipeline, which is a software supply-chain manipulation point: a tampered state file distributed via the next highstate run can silently reconfigure or backdoor every minion it applies to.

data_sources.name: SaltStack Config Audit Log
data_sources.description: State/pillar file modification events with change-source (pipeline vs. direct).

detection_logic: Filters state/pillar file modification events where change_source is not the expected version-control pipeline.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_config_audit_sourcetype> event="FileModified"
| where change_source!="pipeline"
| table _time, user, file_path, change_source
tuning_guidance: Requires the file server to log a change-source attribute distinguishing pipeline-driven syncs from direct edits; alert on all direct edits.
investigation_steps: Diff the file content against the last known-good version-controlled state.
Determine every minion this state/pillar applies to.
response_guidance: Revert to the version-controlled source immediately and re-run highstate.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt External Pillar or GitFS Remote Changed
description: The Salt Master's ext_pillar source or gitfs_remotes configuration was changed to point at a different repository/endpoint, which — like AUTO-010's Git integration equivalent — allows an attacker to control the full content of states/pillars synced from that source.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Master configuration-change events for gitfs_remotes/ext_pillar settings.

detection_logic: Filters master configuration-change events for gitfs_remotes/ext_pillar settings.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="MasterConfigChanged" setting IN ("gitfs_remotes","ext_pillar")
| table _time, user, setting, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the supply-chain severity.
investigation_steps: Verify the new source is the authorized organizational repository.
Audit state/pillar content synced since the change.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Master eauth/External Authentication Configuration Weakened
description: The Salt Master's external authentication (eauth) configuration was modified to grant a user or group broader command-execution permissions than previously held, or a new eauth backend was added, expanding who can issue remote-execution commands against the fleet.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: eauth configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters eauth configuration-change events for review.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="EauthConfigChanged"
| table _time, user, eauth_target, permissions
tuning_guidance: Confirm against access-request tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the change against an approved request.
Review the newly-permitted principal's subsequent command activity.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Minion Reports Command from Unrecognized Master
description: A Salt minion's logs show it accepted a job/command from a master key fingerprint that does not match the organization's known-legitimate Salt Master, consistent with a rogue master impersonation attack (an attacker standing up a competing master and getting a minion to trust it).

data_sources.name: Salt Minion Log
data_sources.description: Master-connection events with master key fingerprint.

detection_logic: Filters minion master-connection events where the fingerprint does not match the known-legitimate master fingerprint.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_minion_sourcetype> event="MasterConnected"
| lookup known_master_fingerprints.csv master_fingerprint OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, minion_id, master_fingerprint
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained known-master-fingerprint lookup; critical during any master key rotation to avoid false positives.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Isolate the affected minion pending investigation.
response_guidance: Remove trust in the rogue master and re-key the minion against the legitimate master.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Job Cache Cleared or Job Return Suppressed
description: The Salt job cache was manually cleared, or a job was run with the --no-return flag against a broad target, both of which suppress the audit trail of what commands were executed against the fleet and what they returned.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Job-cache clear events and job-execution events with return-suppression flags.

detection_logic: Filters job-cache clear events and job-execution events with no_return set.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event IN ("JobCacheCleared") OR (event="JobExecuted" no_return=true)
| table _time, user, action
tuning_guidance: Alert on all job-cache clear events; no_return usage is more common in noisy fire-and-forget automation and needs baselining.
investigation_steps: Determine what was in the job cache before it was cleared, from any available backup/export.
Review the user's other recent activity for signs of anti-forensics.
response_guidance: Treat as a precursor to further undetected malicious command execution.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SaltStack Config RBAC Role Escalated to Super User
description: A user was granted the SaltStack Config super-user role, providing full administrative control over Salt Master configuration, minion key management, and remote-execution permissions through the VCF Automation UI/API layer.

data_sources.name: SaltStack Config Audit Log
data_sources.description: Role-assignment events with role name.

detection_logic: Filters role-assignment events where the granted role is super-user/admin.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_config_audit_sourcetype> event="RoleAssigned" role="SuperUser"
| table _time, actor, target_user, role
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; correlate with change-management approval.
investigation_steps: Confirm the grant against an approved access request.
Review the target account's subsequent activity.
response_guidance: Revoke if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Reactor Configuration Added Triggering Command Execution on Event
description: A Salt Reactor configuration was added binding an event-bus tag to an automatic execution/state action, which — like VCF Automation's extensibility subscriptions — creates a persistence mechanism that automatically re-executes on every future occurrence of the bound event, without requiring further interactive access.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Reactor configuration-change events with bound event tag and reaction.

detection_logic: Filters reactor configuration-addition events for review.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="ReactorConfigChanged" action="added"
| table _time, user, event_tag, reaction
tuning_guidance: Reactor configuration changes are rare in most environments outside initial platform setup; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Review the bound reaction's content and origin.
Determine what event tags will trigger it and how often.
response_guidance: Remove the reactor configuration if the reaction is malicious.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1546: Event Triggered Execution

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Master Publish Port / Network Exposure Changed
description: The Salt Master's publish port or bind interface configuration was changed, potentially exposing the master's command channel to a broader network than intended (e.g. binding to 0.0.0.0 instead of a management-only interface).

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Master network-binding configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters master configuration-change events for interface/bind-address settings.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="MasterConfigChanged" setting="interface"
| table _time, user, setting, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Confirm against network change tickets.
investigation_steps: Verify the new bind address matches the intended management-network scope.
Check firewall rules governing reachability to the new bind address.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Minion Key Deleted or Master Trust Revoked at Scale
description: A large number of minion keys were deleted/rejected in a short window, which — while occasionally a legitimate fleet-decommission action — can also be a denial-of-service against configuration management: severing the master's ability to manage or remediate the affected minions.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Key deletion/rejection events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts key deletion/rejection events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event IN ("KeyDeleted","KeyRejected")
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count values(minion_id) AS minions by _time, user
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Correlate with decommission tickets for legitimate fleet-retirement projects.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a decommission plan.
Treat as a live incident absent one.
response_guidance: Re-establish trust for affected minions if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Command Return Data Contains Credential-Like Content in Job Cache
description: A remote-execution job's returned data, stored in the job cache, contains content matching credential/secret patterns — since the job cache is broadly readable by Salt Master operators, this represents an unintentional credential-exposure surface that an attacker with job-cache read access could harvest from.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.path: Salt Master job cache return data
data_sources.description: Job return payloads matched against a credential-pattern regex.

detection_logic: Filters job-cache return-data content matching credential/secret keyword or format patterns.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="JobReturned"
| where match(return_data, "(?i)(BEGIN (RSA|EC) PRIVATE KEY|password\s*[:=]|api_key\s*[:=])")
| table _time, job_id, minion_id
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate from routine config-dump commands; scope to jobs run by non-automation accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm the specific command and whether credential exposure was intentional/expected.
Rotate any exposed credentials.
response_guidance: Purge the sensitive job return from the cache if policy allows and rotate exposed credentials.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Orchestrate Runner Executed Against Production Environment
description: A Salt orchestrate runner (multi-minion, multi-step orchestration) was executed against an environment tagged production, warranting review given orchestrate's ability to sequence complex multi-host actions beyond a single state.apply.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Orchestrate runner execution events joined against an environment tag lookup.

detection_logic: Filters orchestrate runner-execution events where the target environment is production, joined against a change-window lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="RunnerExecuted" runner="state.orchestrate" environment="production"
| lookup maintenance_windows.csv _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window) OR in_window=0
| table _time, user, orchestrate_name, environment
tuning_guidance: Requires an environment tag and maintenance-window lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review the orchestrate definition's content for unexpected steps.
response_guidance: Halt further execution if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Compromise-to-Fleet-Impact Correlation
description: The named Salt-compromise attack chain: a trust/key change (SALT-003/SALT-004/SALT-008), followed by state or command execution against a broad target (SALT-005/SALT-006), followed by wildcard/mass targeting affecting a large number of minions, combined with a security-control change (e.g. disabling logging, SALT-011) — this sequence indicates the Salt Master has been weaponized to compromise the fleet it manages, the single highest-impact attack path in the entire VCF stack given Salt's fleet-wide command reach.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.path: Correlated key/trust, execution, and logging events for the same actor.
data_sources.description: Multi-stage correlation across SALT-003/004/008, SALT-005/006, and SALT-011.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) a key/trust-change event, (2) a broad-target execution event, (3) a logging/job-cache-tampering event — all for the same actor within a 60-minute window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype>
| eval stage=case(event IN ("KeyAccepted","MasterConfigChanged"), "1_trust", event="JobExecuted" AND match(target,"^\*"), "2_execution", event="JobCacheCleared", "3_evasion")
| where isnotnull(stage)
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by actor
| where stage_count>=2 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=3600
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; this is the flagship chain for VCF Salt and should be a Tier-1 alert given the blast radius.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed fleet-wide incident.
Immediately isolate the Salt Master from the minion network if feasible.
Enumerate every minion that received a job during stage 2 and inspect each for compromise.
response_guidance: Full incident response: rotate Salt Master keys, re-key all minions, audit every state/pillar file, and assume every minion that executed a job during the window may be compromised.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: SaltStack Config Environment/Target Group Definition Broadened
description: A target group (nodegroup) definition used to scope Salt commands to a subset of the fleet was modified to include a broader minion match pattern, which can cause subsequent commands issued against that group to unexpectedly reach a wider set of hosts than the operator intends.

data_sources.name: SaltStack Config Audit Log
data_sources.description: Nodegroup definition modification events.

detection_logic: Filters nodegroup modification events for manual review of scope changes.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_config_audit_sourcetype> event="NodegroupModified"
| table _time, user, nodegroup_name, old_pattern, new_pattern
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate fleet-topology changes.
investigation_steps: Confirm the new pattern's scope is intentional.
Review commands issued against this nodegroup since the change.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Salt Master TLS/Encryption Configuration Weakened
description: The Salt Master's transport encryption configuration was weakened (e.g. disabling the AES-based transport encryption or downgrading to a weaker cipher), which can expose the master-minion command channel to interception or tampering.

data_sources.name: Salt Master Log
data_sources.description: Encryption/transport configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters master configuration-change events for transport/encryption-related settings moving to a weaker value.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<salt_master_sourcetype> event="MasterConfigChanged" setting IN ("transport","ssl")
| table _time, user, setting, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences given the rarity and security impact of transport-encryption changes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess whether the master-minion channel is exposed to untrusted networks.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Site Pairing Established with Unrecognized Remote Site
description: An HCX Connector established a site pairing with a remote HCX Cloud/Connector endpoint that does not match a known-authorized site inventory, potentially establishing an encrypted extension tunnel to an attacker-controlled environment.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: Site-pairing creation events with remote site URL.

detection_logic: Filters site-pairing creation events where the remote site URL does not match a known-authorized site lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="SitePairingCreated"
| lookup known_hcx_sites.csv remote_site_url OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, local_site, remote_site_url
tuning_guidance: Maintain a known-site inventory; multi-cloud/multi-datacenter environments need this actively curated.
investigation_steps: Verify the remote site is an authorized, newly-onboarded environment.
If not, treat as attacker-established infrastructure.
response_guidance: Remove the site pairing immediately if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Service Mesh Deployed with Broad Network Extension Scope
description: An HCX Network Extension was configured to stretch a broad/sensitive Layer-2 segment across the site pairing, which — since network extension bridges the segment across both sites at Layer 2 — can allow lateral movement between environments that were previously network-isolated from each other.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.path: HCX Manager network extension config log
data_sources.description: Network extension creation events with extended segment identity.

detection_logic: Filters network-extension creation events joined against a sensitive-segment tag lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="NetworkExtensionCreated"
| lookup sensitive_segments.csv segment_name OUTPUT is_sensitive
| where is_sensitive=1
| table _time, user, segment_name, remote_site
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained sensitive-segment tag lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for extending this specific segment.
Assess the security posture of the remote site the segment is being extended to.
response_guidance: Remove the extension if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1210: Exploitation of Remote Services

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Bulk Migration Initiated for Large Number of VMs
description: An HCX bulk migration was initiated moving an unusually large number of VMs to a remote site in a short window, which — if the destination or the initiating account is not legitimate — can be used to exfiltrate an entire workload fleet's VMs (including their disks and data) to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: Migration job-initiation events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts VMs included in migration jobs initiated by a single actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="MigrationInitiated"
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats sum(vm_count) AS total_vms values(destination_site) AS destinations by _time, user
| where total_vms>=10
tuning_guidance: Raise the threshold for known, scheduled datacenter-migration projects.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and destination legitimacy.
If unauthorized, treat as active mass exfiltration and halt the migration.
response_guidance: Cancel in-progress migration jobs immediately if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1537: Transfer Data to Cloud Account

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Migration Destination Outside Known Site Inventory
description: A migration job's destination site does not match the organization's known-authorized HCX site inventory, the highest-confidence signal of VM exfiltration via HCX regardless of migration volume.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: Migration job destination joined against a known-site lookup.

detection_logic: Filters migration job events where destination_site does not match the known-site inventory.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="MigrationInitiated"
| lookup known_hcx_sites.csv destination_site OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, user, vm_name, destination_site
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences; this should only ever fire during a legitimate new-site onboarding, which should itself be a tracked change.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live exfiltration incident.
Halt the migration immediately.
response_guidance: Cancel the migration and isolate the initiating account.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Appliance Root/Admin Credential Reset
description: The HCX Manager or HCX Cloud appliance's administrative credential was reset, which — since HCX Manager holds trust relationships to both sites in a pairing — represents a significant persistence/credential-access target.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: Admin credential reset events.

detection_logic: Filters admin credential-reset events on HCX appliances.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="AdminCredentialReset"
| table _time, actor, appliance
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for legitimate credential rotation.
investigation_steps: Confirm the reset was performed by an authorized administrator.
Review subsequent logins and site-pairing/migration activity.
response_guidance: Reset again through the proper channel if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX WAN Optimization/Traffic Engineering Bypass Enabled
description: HCX's WAN optimization or traffic-engineering profile was changed to bypass inspection/shaping for a service mesh, which is generally a low-severity operational change but can be reviewed as part of broader network-path scrutiny.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.path: HCX Manager network profile config log
data_sources.description: Traffic-engineering profile change events.

detection_logic: Lists traffic-engineering profile change events for periodic review.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="TrafficEngineeringChanged"
| table _time, user, service_mesh, setting
tuning_guidance: Low standalone value; primarily useful for periodic configuration-drift review.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Mobility Optimized Networking Policy Disabled
description: Mobility Optimized Networking (MON), which allows migrated VMs to route locally rather than tromboning traffic back through the source site, was disabled for a network extension — while primarily a performance setting, unexpected changes here warrant confirmation given their effect on traffic paths for migrated workloads.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: MON policy disable events.

detection_logic: Filters MON policy status-change events where the new status is disabled.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="MonPolicyChanged" status="disabled"
| table _time, user, segment_name, status
tuning_guidance: Confirm against network-design change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Assess resulting traffic-path change for migrated VMs on this segment.
response_guidance: Re-enable if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Migration of VM Tagged as Highly Sensitive
description: An HCX migration job included a VM tagged as highly sensitive/regulated data, warranting the highest scrutiny regardless of destination legitimacy given the data-protection implications of moving such a workload across sites (and potentially across compliance/jurisdiction boundaries).

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: Migration job events joined against a sensitive-VM tag lookup.

detection_logic: Joins migration job events against a sensitive-VM tag lookup.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="MigrationInitiated"
| lookup sensitive_vm_tags.csv vm_name OUTPUT is_sensitive
| where is_sensitive=1
| table _time, user, vm_name, destination_site
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained sensitive-VM tag lookup; high value once available given compliance stakes.
investigation_steps: Confirm business/compliance justification and approval for this specific VM's migration.
Verify the destination site meets the same data-protection/jurisdiction requirements.
response_guidance: Halt the migration pending compliance review if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1537: Transfer Data to Cloud Account

author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Site Pairing Removed Then Re-Established with Different Certificate
description: A site pairing was removed and re-established shortly afterward presenting a different remote-site certificate than before, which can indicate an attacker performing an adversary-in-the-middle takeover of a trusted site relationship.

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: Site-pairing removal and creation events with certificate thumbprints.

detection_logic: Correlates a pairing-removal event followed by a pairing-creation event for the same remote site URL within a short window where the certificate thumbprint differs.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("SitePairingRemoved","SitePairingCreated")
| transaction remote_site_url maxspan=30m startswith=eval(event=="SitePairingRemoved") endswith=eval(event=="SitePairingCreated")
| where mvcount(cert_thumbprint)>1
| table _time, user, remote_site_url, cert_thumbprint
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented certificate-rotation change ticket for the remote site.
investigation_steps: Verify the new certificate belongs to the legitimate remote site's HCX Cloud/Connector appliance.
If not, treat as an active adversary-in-the-middle incident.
response_guidance: Remove the pairing immediately and re-establish only after out-of-band certificate verification.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: HCX Replication-Assisted vMotion (RAV) Used for High-Volume Cross-Site Data Movement
description: HCX Replication-Assisted vMotion moved an unusually large aggregate data volume across a site pairing in a short window, a subtler variant of HCX-003 that surfaces high-volume data movement even when VM counts are low (e.g. a small number of very large VMs).

data_sources.name: HCX Manager Log
data_sources.description: RAV migration events with transferred data volume.

detection_logic: Sums data volume transferred via RAV per actor within a rolling window and flags totals above a threshold.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event="RavMigrationCompleted"
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats sum(data_volume_gb) AS total_gb by _time, user
| eventstats avg(total_gb) AS avg_gb stdev(total_gb) AS stdev_gb by user
| where total_gb > (avg_gb + 3*stdev_gb)
tuning_guidance: Baseline per user; large legitimate migration projects will need a temporary allowlist.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the migration project.
Cross-check against HCX-003/HCX-004 for destination legitimacy.
response_guidance: Investigate if unjustified.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1537: Transfer Data to Cloud Account

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Tanzu Supervisor Cluster Admin ClusterRoleBinding Created
description: A ClusterRoleBinding granting cluster-admin (or an equivalent broad role) was created on the Supervisor Cluster or a Tanzu Kubernetes Grid guest cluster, granting full API-server control over the cluster and, via the Supervisor's integration with vSphere, potential influence over the underlying infrastructure.

data_sources.name: Kubernetes Audit Log
data_sources.description: ClusterRoleBinding creation events referencing cluster-admin.

detection_logic: Filters ClusterRoleBinding creation events where roleRef is cluster-admin.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<k8s_audit_sourcetype> verb="create" objectRef.resource="clusterrolebindings"
| where responseObject.roleRef.name="cluster-admin"
| table _time, user, responseObject.metadata.name, responseObject.subjects
tuning_guidance: Confirm against access-request tickets; cluster-admin grants should be rare and tightly controlled.
investigation_steps: Verify the grant against an approved request.
Review the subject's subsequent API activity.
response_guidance: Revoke if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Tanzu Cluster Privileged Pod Created
description: A pod was created with securityContext.privileged=true (or hostPID/hostNetwork/hostPath mounts), granting it access to the underlying node's kernel and filesystem — a container-escape-enabling configuration that can lead to compromise of the worker node itself.

data_sources.name: Kubernetes Audit Log
data_sources.description: Pod creation events with privileged security context.

detection_logic: Filters pod-creation events where any container's securityContext sets privileged=true.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<k8s_audit_sourcetype> verb="create" objectRef.resource="pods"
| where requestObject.spec.containers{}.securityContext.privileged=true
| table _time, user, requestObject.metadata.name, requestObject.metadata.namespace
tuning_guidance: Some legitimate infrastructure DaemonSets (CNI, storage drivers) require privileged pods; maintain a namespace/name allowlist.
investigation_steps: Verify the pod is a known, allowlisted infrastructure component.
If not, treat as a container-escape attempt and inspect the node for compromise.
response_guidance: Delete the pod immediately if unauthorized; apply a Pod Security Standard policy to prevent recurrence.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1611: Escape to Host

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Tanzu Cluster Secret Accessed at Unusual Volume
description: A service account or user retrieved an unusually large number of Kubernetes Secret objects in a short window, consistent with an attacker who has gained API access enumerating and harvesting every credential stored in the cluster.

data_sources.name: Kubernetes Audit Log
data_sources.description: Secret get/list events aggregated per actor per window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct Secret get/list events per actor within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<k8s_audit_sourcetype> verb IN ("get","list") objectRef.resource="secrets"
| bucket _time span=10m
| stats dc(objectRef.name) AS secret_count by _time, user
| where secret_count>=20
tuning_guidance: Exclude known controller/operator service accounts with legitimate broad secret access.
investigation_steps: Identify the actor and whether it is a known controller.
If not, treat as credential-harvesting and rotate all accessed secrets.
response_guidance: Revoke the actor's API access and rotate exposed secrets.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Tanzu Cluster Service Account Token Used from Outside Cluster Network
description: A Kubernetes service account token was used to authenticate to the API server from a source IP address outside the expected in-cluster/management network range, suggesting the token was exfiltrated (e.g. via container filesystem access) and is being used externally.

data_sources.name: Kubernetes Audit Log
data_sources.description: API server authentication events with source IP, filtered to service-account identities.

detection_logic: Filters API server access events authenticated via a service account token where the source IP falls outside the expected in-cluster CIDR.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<k8s_audit_sourcetype> user.username="system:serviceaccount:*"
| where NOT cidrmatch("<cluster_pod_cidr>", src_ip)
| table _time, user, src_ip
tuning_guidance: Some service accounts legitimately authenticate from CI/CD runners outside the pod CIDR; maintain an allowlist for those.
investigation_steps: Determine how the token could have left the cluster (e.g. compromised pod, exposed ConfigMap/log).
Revoke and rotate the token.
response_guidance: Rotate the service account token and audit the pod it was originally mounted to.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Tanzu Supervisor Namespace Resource Quota Removed
description: A vSphere Namespace's resource quota (CPU/memory/storage limits mapped from the vCenter-managed namespace) was removed or significantly increased, potentially allowing a compromised or malicious workload in that namespace to consume disproportionate cluster resources.

data_sources.name: vCenter Event
data_sources.description: Namespace resource-limit configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters namespace resource-limit change events where limits are removed or substantially increased.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vcenter.namespaces.ResourceLimitsChanged"
| table _time, user, namespace, old_limits, new_limits
tuning_guidance: Confirm against capacity-planning change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Monitor for resource-exhaustion activity within the affected namespace afterward.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Tanzu Cluster Admission Controller/Webhook Disabled
description: A ValidatingWebhookConfiguration or MutatingWebhookConfiguration (e.g. one enforcing Pod Security Standards or an OPA/Gatekeeper policy) was deleted or disabled, removing an admission-time security control before subsequent workload deployments.

data_sources.name: Kubernetes Audit Log
data_sources.description: Webhook configuration deletion events.

detection_logic: Filters webhook configuration deletion events.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<k8s_audit_sourcetype> verb="delete" objectRef.resource IN ("validatingwebhookconfigurations","mutatingwebhookconfigurations")
| table _time, user, objectRef.name
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences for security-critical webhooks (identified via a naming-convention or annotation lookup); routine for non-security webhooks during normal operations.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review what workloads were deployed while the control was disabled.
response_guidance: Restore immediately if unauthorized and audit workloads admitted during the gap.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Tanzu Cluster Exec Into Pod in Sensitive Namespace
description: A user executed an interactive shell session into a running pod (kubectl exec) within a namespace tagged as sensitive/production, warranting review given the direct container-access this grants.

data_sources.name: Kubernetes Audit Log
data_sources.description: Pod exec subresource-access events joined against a sensitive-namespace tag lookup.

detection_logic: Filters pods/exec subresource-access events joined against a sensitive-namespace lookup.
spl:

title: Ransomware Kill-Chain: Privileged Auth to Storage Destruction
description: The flagship VCF ransomware kill-chain: privileged authentication to vCenter/ESXi, followed by direct ESXi host access, followed by SSH/Shell enablement, followed by a security or logging control being impaired, followed by mass VM power-off, followed by snapshot deletion, followed by VMDK/datastore manipulation, culminating in host/storage unavailability — this correlation strings together signals from the base ESXi/vCenter catalogue with VSAN-005/VSAN-007 to catch the full sequence even when individual stage detections are tuned down.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: vCenter events + ESXi shell/SSH logs + vSAN disk-group events for the same actor/session
data_sources.description: Six-stage correlation: auth, host access, shell enablement, control impairment, mass power-off, storage destruction.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring stages in approximate order: (1) privileged auth, (2) direct ESXi access, (3) SSH/Shell enabled, (4) security control disabled (lockdown/syslog/firewall), (5) mass VM power-off, (6) snapshot/VMDK/disk-group destruction — for the same actor/session within a 2-hour window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> (sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> OR sourcetype=<esxi_shell_sourcetype> OR sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype>)
| eval stage=case(
    event_type="com.vmware.sso.PrivilegedLogin", "1_auth",
    event_type="esxi.ssh.enabled", "2_shell",
    event_type IN ("esxi.lockdown.disabled","esxi.syslog.changed"), "3_control_impaired",
    event_type="com.vmware.vc.vm.PoweredOff", "4_poweroff",
    event_type IN ("com.vmware.vc.vm.SnapshotDeleted","com.vmware.vsan.diskgroup.removed"), "5_storage_destroyed")
| where isnotnull(stage)
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count count(eval(stage="4_poweroff")) AS poweroff_count by actor
| where stage_count>=3 AND poweroff_count>=5 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=7200
tuning_guidance: This is a Tier-1 correlation search requiring an SIEM with cross-source correlation (Splunk ES or equivalent). Tune stage_count and poweroff_count thresholds to environment size.
investigation_steps: Treat any match as a confirmed active ransomware/destructive incident.
Immediately isolate the actor's account and any hosts touched.
Engage full incident response and begin recovery-point assessment from backups.
response_guidance: Activate the incident response ransomware playbook: isolate affected hosts/clusters from the network, halt the actor's session, and begin recovery from the most recent clean backup.

title: Management-Plane-Compromise Chain: Identity to Multi-Host Impact
description: The named management-plane-compromise chain: identity compromise (unusual/anomalous authentication), followed by vCenter or SDDC Manager access, followed by role/permission escalation, followed by API/automation activity, culminating in multiple hosts or VMs being affected — this correlation catches an attacker who pivots from a compromised identity into fleet-wide impact via the SDDC management plane, before any single-stage detection alone would justify a Critical-severity response.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: SDDC Manager + vCenter authentication, RBAC, and API events for the same actor
data_sources.description: Four-stage correlation: identity anomaly, management access, privilege escalation, multi-object API activity.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) an authentication anomaly (new source/impossible travel/success-after-failure), (2) SDDC Manager or vCenter admin login, (3) a role/privilege-escalation event, (4) API activity touching >=5 distinct objects — for the same actor within a 90-minute window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index>
| eval stage=case(
    event="SuccessAfterFailureBurst" OR event="ImpossibleTravel", "1_identity_anomaly",
    event_type="com.vmware.sso.PrivilegedLogin" OR sourcetype=<sddc_audit_sourcetype>, "2_mgmt_access",
    event IN ("RoleGranted","PrivilegeEscalation"), "3_escalation",
    event="ApiCallExecuted", "4_api_activity")
| where isnotnull(stage)
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count dc(object_id) AS object_count by actor
| where stage_count>=3 AND object_count>=5 AND (last_seen-first_seen)<=5400
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; the flagship management-plane chain and a Tier-1 alert candidate.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed incident.
Enumerate every object touched via the API activity stage.
Suspend the actor's credentials across both SDDC Manager and vCenter.
response_guidance: Full incident response: credential rotation, session termination, and audit of every object modified during stage 4.

title: NSX-Segmentation-Bypass Chain: Admin Login to Lateral Traffic
description: The named NSX-segmentation-bypass chain: an NSX admin login, followed by a security group or firewall rule change, followed by a new allowed network path being created, followed by previously-blocked east-west traffic subsequently flowing through it — this correlation ties NSX-001/NSX-002 authentication signals to NSX-011/NSX-013 firewall changes to NSX-031 flow-data evidence, confirming that a policy change was actually exploited rather than merely made.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: NSX Manager audit log (auth + DFW/group changes) joined with NSX flow logs for the same time window
data_sources.description: Three-stage correlation: admin login, firewall/group change, subsequent flow matching the new path.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring: (1) NSX admin login, (2) a DFW rule or security-group change broadening scope, (3) a subsequent flow record between the newly-connected segments — for the same actor/scope within a 60-minute window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype>
| eval stage=case(event="AuthenticationSuccess" AND role="Enterprise Admin", "1_admin_login", event IN ("DfwRuleModified","GroupCriteriaChanged"), "2_policy_change")
| where isnotnull(stage)
| stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(stage) AS stages dc(stage) AS stage_count by actor
| where stage_count>=2
| join type=inner [search index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<nsx_flow_sourcetype> | lookup segmentation_intent_matrix.csv source_segment, dest_segment OUTPUT allowed | where allowed=0]
tuning_guidance: Requires both NSX audit and flow-log correlation support; high-value once the segmentation-intent matrix lookup is in place.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed segmentation-bypass incident.
Identify what traffic actually traversed the new path and to what destination.
Revert the policy change immediately.
response_guidance: Revert the firewall/group change, investigate both communicating endpoints for compromise, and review the admin account for unauthorized use.

title: Rogue DHCP/Network-Layer Precursor to VCF Management-Plane Attack
description: A rogue DHCP server or ARP-spoofing indicator was detected on the management network segment (via the DHCP-### catalogue's DHCP-052/DHCP-053-style detections) shortly before an unusual authentication event against SDDC Manager, vCenter, or NSX Manager, consistent with an on-path attacker using management-network MITM to intercept or replay management-plane credentials.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Network-layer rogue-DHCP/ARP-spoof alerts correlated with management-plane authentication events on the same subnet within a short window
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: network-layer MITM indicator, followed by management-plane authentication anomaly.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a rogue-DHCP/ARP-spoof alert on the management VLAN followed by an authentication anomaly against SDDC Manager/vCenter/NSX Manager on the same subnet within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> (sourcetype=<dhcp_audit_sourcetype> OR sourcetype=<network_ids_sourcetype>) event IN ("RogueDhcpDetected","ArpSpoofDetected") vlan="<mgmt_vlan>"
| join type=inner subnet [search index=<vcf_index> (sourcetype=<sddc_audit_sourcetype> OR sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> OR sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype>) event="AuthenticationSuccess" | eval subnet=mvindex(split(src_ip,"."),0,2)]
| where (_time_auth - _time) <= 1800 AND (_time_auth - _time) >= 0
tuning_guidance: Requires network-layer rogue-DHCP/ARP-spoof detection capability (see the companion DHCP catalogue) feeding the same SIEM as VCF telemetry.
investigation_steps: Treat as a possible on-path credential-interception incident against the management plane.
Force credential rotation for any accounts that authenticated during the exposure window.
response_guidance: Isolate the rogue device, rotate potentially-intercepted credentials, and review the management network's physical/switch-port security.

title: KMS-Compromise-to-Encryption-Impact Chain
description: A KMS trust/cluster configuration change (VSAN-002) was followed by a data-at-rest encryption change (VSAN-001) or an unscheduled deep rekey (VSAN-003) on one or more vSAN clusters, consistent with an attacker who compromised the key-management relationship using it to either disable encryption ahead of a data-theft operation or to induce a crypto-shredding denial-of-service by rotating to keys the legitimate organization cannot recover.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: vCenter KMS cluster-change events followed by vSAN encryption/rekey events for the same cluster
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: KMS trust change, followed by an encryption-state change on the same cluster.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a KMS cluster-configuration-change event followed by a vSAN encryption-disable or unscheduled-rekey event on the same cluster within 24 hours.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type="com.vmware.vc.kms.ClusterChanged"
| join type=inner cluster [search index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> event_type IN ("com.vmware.vsan.encryption.changed","com.vmware.vsan.rekey.started")]
| where (_time_encryption - _time) <= 86400 AND (_time_encryption - _time) >= 0
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches given the criticality of both individual stages.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed incident.
Verify the KMS endpoint's authenticity and the encryption keys' integrity.
Halt any in-progress rekey/decrypt operation if unauthorized.
response_guidance: Full incident response: revert KMS trust to the known-good endpoint, verify all encryption keys are recoverable, and audit data access during the exposure window.

title: Content-Library/Software-Supply-Chain Attack Chain
description: A software-supply-chain surface (SDDC Manager software depot config, VCF Lifecycle Manager bundle checksum mismatch, a Content Library subscription source, an Automation blueprint Git remote, or a Salt gitfs remote) was reconfigured to point at an unrecognized source, followed by content being deployed/synced from it and subsequently applied at scale — this correlation unifies the supply-chain detections spread across VCF-024, AUTO-010, and SALT-008 into a single named chain per the master prompt's explicit supply-chain framing.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Software depot / Git remote / gitfs remote configuration-change events followed by mass content-application events across any of the source platforms
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: supply-chain source reconfigured, followed by mass deployment/application from it.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a source-reconfiguration event (VCF-024/AUTO-010/SALT-008-style) followed by a mass deployment/state-application event on the same platform within 24 hours.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> event IN ("DepotConfigChanged","GitIntegrationChanged","MasterConfigChanged")
| where (event="MasterConfigChanged" AND setting IN ("gitfs_remotes","ext_pillar")) OR event IN ("DepotConfigChanged","GitIntegrationChanged")
| join type=inner actor [search index=<vcf_index> event IN ("DeploymentRequested","JobExecuted","BundleImported") | bucket _time span=1d | stats count by actor, _time | where count>=10]
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation across SDDC Manager, Automation, and Salt telemetry in the same SIEM; a strong Tier-1 candidate given the breadth of impact a poisoned supply-chain source can have.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed incident.
Audit all content deployed/applied from the reconfigured source since the change.
Identify the full blast radius across every platform the poisoned content reached.
response_guidance: Revert the source configuration, quarantine/redeploy affected workloads/states, and conduct a full supply-chain compromise assessment.

title: HCX-Enabled Cross-Site Exfiltration Following Management Compromise
description: A management-plane privilege-escalation event (VCF-X-002-style) was followed by HCX site-pairing or migration activity to an unrecognized destination (HCX-001/HCX-004) within a short window, consistent with an attacker who escalated privileges specifically to abuse HCX's legitimate cross-site data-movement capability for bulk exfiltration.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Management-plane privilege-escalation events followed by HCX site-pairing/migration events for the same actor
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: privilege escalation, followed by HCX exfiltration activity.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a role/privilege-escalation event followed by an HCX site-pairing-to-unrecognized-site or migration-to-unrecognized-destination event for the same actor within 4 hours.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> event IN ("RoleGranted","PrivilegeEscalation")
| join type=inner actor [search index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<hcx_audit_sourcetype> event IN ("SitePairingCreated","MigrationInitiated") | lookup known_hcx_sites.csv remote_site_url OUTPUT is_known | where isnull(is_known)]
| where (_time_hcx - _time) <= 14400 AND (_time_hcx - _time) >= 0
tuning_guidance: Requires correlation-search support; high-confidence given both individual stages already carry strong signal.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed exfiltration incident.
Halt any in-progress migration and remove the rogue site pairing.
Determine what data/VMs left the environment before detection.
response_guidance: Full incident response: revoke escalated privileges, terminate the HCX session, and assess data-loss scope.

title: Anti-Forensics Chain: Coordinated Logging Impairment Across VCF Components
description: Logging/forwarding/retention was impaired on two or more distinct VCF components (any combination of NSX-034, LOGS-002/LOGS-004, K8S-009, SALT-011, or the base ESXi syslog/lockdown detections) within a short window, consistent with an attacker methodically blinding every telemetry source across the SDDC before conducting further undetected activity.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Logging/audit-impairment events across NSX, VCF Operations for Logs, Tanzu, Salt, and ESXi for the same actor or timeframe
data_sources.description: Threshold correlation: distinct logging-impairment events across >=2 components within a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct components with a logging/audit-impairment event within a rolling window, regardless of whether the same actor performed each (coordinated multi-account attacks are in scope).
spl:
index=<vcf_index> event IN ("SyslogExporterChanged","RetentionPolicyChanged","ForwarderChanged","AuditPolicyChanged","JobCacheCleared") OR event_type IN ("esxi.syslog.changed","esxi.lockdown.disabled")
| bucket _time span=2h
| stats dc(component) AS component_count values(component) AS components values(actor) AS actors by _time
| where component_count>=2
tuning_guidance: Correlate with a declared platform-wide maintenance window (e.g. a logging-infrastructure migration) to suppress planned exceptions.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed coordinated anti-forensics incident absent a maintenance ticket.
Immediately restore logging across every affected component.
Widen the investigation scope to assume broader compromise given the deliberate blinding.
response_guidance: Restore all impaired logging, then conduct a full incident investigation using whatever telemetry remains plus any independent backup/export sources.

title: DHCP Starvation/Rogue-DHCP Precursor to VCF Host Provisioning Compromise
description: A rogue DHCP or DHCP-starvation indicator on the management/provisioning network (per the companion DHCP catalogue) preceded an SDDC Manager host-commissioning event, consistent with an attacker manipulating DHCP-assigned network configuration (e.g. gateway/DNS options) to intercept or redirect traffic from a newly-commissioned ESXi host before it is fully hardened.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Network-layer rogue-DHCP/starvation alerts followed by an SDDC Manager host-commission event on the same subnet
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: DHCP-layer network attack indicator, followed by host provisioning on the affected subnet.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a rogue-DHCP/DHCP-starvation alert on the provisioning VLAN followed by a host-commissioning event on the same subnet within 6 hours.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> (sourcetype=<dhcp_audit_sourcetype>) event IN ("RogueDhcpDetected","DhcpStarvationDetected") vlan="<provisioning_vlan>"
| join type=inner subnet [search index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<sddc_audit_sourcetype> event="HostCommissioned" | eval subnet=mvindex(split(host_ip,"."),0,2)]
| where (_time_commission - _time) <= 21600 AND (_time_commission - _time) >= 0
tuning_guidance: Requires network-layer DHCP-attack detection capability feeding the same SIEM as VCF telemetry.
investigation_steps: Treat the newly-commissioned host as potentially compromised at first boot.
Verify the host's actual assigned network configuration against the intended values.
Re-image/re-commission the host if tampering is confirmed.
response_guidance: Isolate the affected host, verify its configuration, and remediate the rogue DHCP source on the provisioning network.

title: VPN-Compromise-to-VCF-Management-Access Chain
description: A VPN authentication anomaly (success-after-failure-burst, or login from a new/unrecognized geography) was followed by a management-plane authentication event against SDDC Manager, vCenter, or NSX Manager from the VPN-assigned address space, consistent with the RDP-catalogue's analogous VPN-compromise-to-RDP chain but targeting the VCF management plane instead of a Windows host.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: VPN authentication-anomaly events followed by VCF management-plane authentication from the VPN address pool
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: VPN compromise indicator, followed by management-plane access from that session.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a VPN authentication anomaly followed by a VCF management-plane login from an IP within the VPN's assigned address pool, for the same user identity, within 2 hours.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> sourcetype=<vpn_audit_sourcetype> event="SuccessAfterFailureBurst"
| join type=inner user [search index=<vcf_index> (sourcetype=<sddc_audit_sourcetype> OR sourcetype=<vcenter_event_sourcetype> OR sourcetype=<nsx_audit_sourcetype>) event="AuthenticationSuccess" | lookup vpn_address_pool.csv src_ip OUTPUT is_vpn_range | where is_vpn_range=1]
| where (_time_mgmt - _time) <= 7200 AND (_time_mgmt - _time) >= 0
tuning_guidance: Requires a VPN address-pool lookup and cross-source correlation support.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed incident given the VPN-compromise precursor.
Suspend the user's VPN and management-plane sessions.
Review all management-plane activity performed during the session.
response_guidance: Full incident response: rotate VPN and management-plane credentials, enforce MFA if not already required, and audit session activity.

title: Fleet-Wide Attack Correlation: Simultaneous Anomalies Across Multiple Workload Domains
description: Critical-severity anomalies (any combination of mass power-off, mass deployment destruction, mass disk-group removal, or mass minion key deletion) were observed across two or more distinct workload domains within a short window, indicating an attack (or automation gone catastrophically wrong) operating at fleet scale rather than against a single isolated cluster.

data_sources.path: Critical-severity destructive events across VSAN-005, AUTO-005, and SALT-015 joined against workload-domain membership
data_sources.description: Threshold correlation: destructive events across >=2 distinct workload domains within a rolling window.

title: Identity-Provider Compromise Correlated Across Every VCF Component
description: The same identity (as resolved through federated SSO) authenticated to three or more distinct VCF component types (any combination of SDDC Manager, vCenter, NSX Manager, VCF Operations, VCF Automation, Salt, HCX) within an unusually short window, which — given how rarely a single legitimate administrator operates across that many planes in quick succession — suggests the identity provider itself may be compromised and the attacker is using single sign-on to pivot broadly before any one platform's own detections catch up.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Federated-identity authentication events across all VCF component audit logs for the same resolved identity
data_sources.description: Threshold correlation: the same federated identity authenticating to >=3 distinct component types within a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct VCF component types a single federated identity authenticated to within a rolling window.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> event="AuthenticationSuccess"
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats dc(component_type) AS component_count values(component_type) AS components by _time, identity
| where component_count>=3
tuning_guidance: Exclude known break-glass/DR-testing scenarios and dedicated platform-engineering accounts that legitimately span multiple components.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether this matches a known operational pattern (e.g. a platform engineer's DR drill).

title: Backup-Infrastructure Compromise Preceding Mass Destructive Activity
description: Backup job configuration was tampered with (disabled, retention shortened, or target changed) shortly before a mass-destruction event elsewhere in the VCF stack (mass VM power-off, disk-group removal, deployment destruction, or Kubernetes cluster deletion), consistent with a deliberate pre-ransomware step of disabling recovery capability before the destructive payload executes — mirroring the base ESXi catalogue's backup-tampering detections but correlated specifically against VCF-wide destructive indicators.

data_sources.name: Correlated Multi-Source Log
data_sources.path: Backup job configuration-change events followed by any mass-destruction event across the VCF stack within a short window
data_sources.description: Two-stage correlation: backup tampering, followed by mass destruction.

detection_logic: Correlation search requiring a backup job disable/retention-shortened/target-changed event followed by any mass-destruction event (VSAN-005, AUTO-005, K8S-010, or base-catalogue mass-power-off/snapshot-deletion) within 12 hours.
spl:
index=<vcf_index> event IN ("BackupJobDisabled","BackupRetentionChanged","BackupTargetChanged")
| join type=inner [search index=<vcf_index> event IN ("MassDiskGroupRemoval","MassDeploymentDestroyed","MassVmPoweredOff","ClusterDeleted")]
| where (_time_destruction - _time) <= 43200 AND (_time_destruction - _time) >= 0
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; this sequence has essentially no legitimate operational explanation.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed ransomware/destructive-attack precursor-and-payload pair.
Immediately verify whether any backup copies remain intact and accessible outside the tampered configuration.
Begin recovery planning from the most recent verified-clean backup.
response_guidance: Activate the full ransomware incident-response and business-continuity plan; do not rely on the tampered backup configuration for recovery.
